items.title: [BugFix][Ops] Zero-init KDA chunked-prefill pipeline buffers
items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The KDA chunked-prefill path allocates intermediate buffers with `torch.empty*`/`new_empty`:
`chunk_delta_h`'s `h` / `final_state` / `v_new`, `chunk_local_cumsum`'s output (x2), and `recompute_w_u`'s `w` / `u` / `kg`.

The triton kernels write **tile-shaped** regions and leave tail elements untouched whenever the sequence length is not tile-aligned. With a pooled caching allocator those unwritten bytes hold whatever a previous launch left there, so:

- **two identical calls can return different recurrent states** (measured on 910B3: 99.3% of final-state elements differing, max |delta| 0.207),
- the final recurrent state — the hand-off that decode builds on — depends on unrelated request history, silently corrupting long-context generation quality.

This PR zero-initializes all eight buffers. The cost is one memset per call, negligible next to the kernel runtimes.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes — long-context generations on KDA-based hybrid models become deterministic and no longer depend on request history (a silent accuracy fix).

### How was this patch tested?

- New UT: `tests/ut/ops/test_kda_chunk_buffer_init.py`
  - `test_chunk_kda_is_deterministic` (771/968/1303-token prefills, 3 identical calls → bitwise-identical output + final state)
  - `test_chunk_kda_survives_allocator_churn` (pool-sized garbage allocated/freed between calls → results unchanged)
  - All 4 tests pass on Atlas 910B3.
- End-to-end on a 48-layer hybrid GLM/KDA model: chunked prefill becomes bitwise deterministic; a 12-problem GSM8K-level gate scores 12/12 after the fix (nondeterministic outputs before it).

items.title: [BugFix][Kernel] Fix equal-length WY indices
items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The equal-length path of `recompute_w_u_fwd_kernel` had three related indexing issues:

- `i_t` was only initialized in the variable-length branch, causing Triton compilation to fail with `NameError: i_t is not defined` when `cu_seqlens=None`;
- the batch index was derived from a loop over `range(H)`, so it was always zero and batched equal-length inputs wrote to batch 0;
- `beta` and `g_cumsum` are transposed to `[B, H, T]`, but their pointers reused the `[B, T, ...]` token offset instead of a batch-head base.

This PR initializes the equal-length chunk and batch indices from the launch grid, uses a separate `B * H * T` base for the transposed tensors, and adds an A2 NPU regression test covering two batches and multiple chunks with distinct per-batch values.

Fixes #14154

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Equal-length calls to `recompute_w_u_fwd` with `cu_seqlens=None` now compile and produce correct results for batched inputs.

### How was this patch tested?

- Ascend 910B3, CANN 9.0.0, vLLM 0.21.0, vLLM Ascend 0.21.0rc1, Torch/TorchNPU 2.10.0:
  - directly ran the regression case with `B=2`, `T=96`, `BT=64`, `Hg=2`, `H=4`, and `K=V=64`;
  - used distinct `beta` and `g_cumsum` values for each batch;
  - the Triton kernel compiled and both `w` and `u` matched the analytical expected outputs.
- `ruff check vllm_ascend/ops/triton/fla/wy_fast.py tests/ut/ops/a2/test_wy_fast.py`
- `ruff format --check vllm_ascend/ops/triton/fla/wy_fast.py tests/ut/ops/a2/test_wy_fast.py`
- `python -m py_compile vllm_ascend/ops/triton/fla/wy_fast.py tests/ut/ops/a2/test_wy_fast.py`
- `git diff --check`
- `python .github/workflows/scripts/coverage.py`
- Local test selection routes `tests/ut/ops/a2/test_wy_fast.py` to the single-card A2 runner.

The release image cannot collect the test against the latest repository `main` because the image contains vLLM 0.21.0 while current `main` targets vLLM 0.27.1. The target kernel was therefore validated on the release-compatible checkout. Runtime validation against the latest main stack will be performed by the selected A2 NPU CI after the `ready` label is added.

items.title: "MegaGDN" kernel enabling 15% faster prefill for Qwen3.5/3.6 models
items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

**3x faster** kernels than existing `chunk_gated_delta_rule` inside [vllm_ascend/ops/triton/fla](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/tree/v0.19.1rc1/vllm_ascend/ops/triton/fla). Measured **15% prefill speed-up (15% less TTFT)** for various Qwen3.5/3.6 models. No accuracy impact as shown by lm-eval. See our [full report](https://github.com/huawei-csl/megagdn-pto/tree/main/blog).

To verify the benefit of this new feature, it's easier to first use the [our "patch" style repo `megagdn-pto`](https://github.com/huawei-csl/megagdn-pto), to avoid rebuilding vllm-ascend from scratch. This PR brings such external patch into vllm-ascend source, for better long-term maintainability.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No, just a faster internal kernel.

### How was this patch tested?

The original standalone [`megagdn-pto` repo](https://github.com/huawei-csl/megagdn-pto) has test scripts for:
- Single-kernel unit tests and benchmarks
- Prefill TTFT benchmark
- lm-eval score evaluation

I can put some of them into this PR. Let me know which are needed.

### Notes for vllm-ascend maintainers

This is the first attempt to merge PTO-ISA kernels into vllm-ascend, so likely need a few rounds of reviews and edits. 

The current way this PR is structured:
- PTO C++ kernels are in `csrc/pto_chunk_gdn/`, the same level of directory as other AscendC kernel sources
- The torch interfaces are under `vllm_ascend/ops/pto_chunk_gdn/`
- I put a feature guide `docs/source/user_guide/feature_guide/enable_megagdn_kernel.md`
- To provide PTO-ISA dependency, I added https://gitcode.com/cann/pto-isa to `csrc/third_party/pto-isa` as git submodule, the same way as the `csrc/third_party/catlass` submodule.
- CANN installation also provides PTO-ISA headers, similar to how it provides AscendC headers. It's located in `$ASCEND_HOME_PATH/include/pto`. But the headers in 8.5.0 is not new enough, thus I pulled a more recent commit. With future newer CANN releases, this `pto-isa` git submodule might not be needed.

Let me know your preferred: (1) code organization (2) compilation procedure (3) if more docs and tests needed. Then we can make further changes to make this PR more "merge-able".

I assume the PTO torch interface needs to be the same as current AscendC build structure? i.e. Using CMake + pybind (torch C++ api). An alternative without needing to rebuild csrc directory, is to use "JIT compile" style, calling `bisheng` + `ctypes` on the fly, so it's more like triton/tilelang's way of invoking kernels.

### Known uncovered cases by this PR

- Kernels are fully tested on Atlas A2, and should also be compatible with A3 (same aicore isa), but I didn't verify directly (no A3 machine)
- A5 & Ascend 950 is not tested *yet*. Although PTO-ISA abstracts away A3 vs A5 differences, we still need slight tweaks to the kernel sources and launch interface (mostly for Cube-Vector communication). This is planned as the next PR (current one is already big enough, don't want to bloat the code)
- Multi-device inference for larger 122B/397B models are not tested yet. Will need to fuse communication to gain best speed-up, otherwise the eager communication calls will kill any single-kernel speed-up. This is planned as future PRs.

## Extended summary 

(below are AI summarized but quite correct; above are purely human written)

<details>

PR: Enable PTO GDN Megakernel for Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.6 prefill

**Target**: `vllm-project/vllm-ascend` main branch

---

## Summary

Integrate fused PTO megakernel for the **chunk GatedDeltaNet (GDN)** used in Qwen3.5 and
Qwen3.6 models, replacing the default Triton implementation during prefill.

Key outcomes:
- **7–25% TTFT reduction** on Ascend 910B, depending on model size and sequence length.
- **Zero accuracy regression**: WikiText PPL and MMLU scores match Triton to floating-point equivalence.
- **Decode unaffected**: the PTO path only activates for prefill (zero `initial_state`); decode transparently falls back to Triton.
- **Single opt-in env var**: `VLLM_ASCEND_PTO_CHUNK_GDN=1`.

---

## Background

Qwen3.5 (0.8B – 9B) and Qwen3.6 (27B, 35B-A3B-MoE) use a **GatedDeltaNet**
recurrent layer that dominates prefill cost at long context lengths.  The
existing Triton-based implementation runs with `chunk_size=64` and BF16.
The new PTO megakernel runs with `chunk_size=128` in FP16 on the Ascend
AI-Core vector unit, fusing all six pipeline stages into a **single NPU dispatch**.

### Pipeline stages (all fused into one kernel launch)

```
Q, K, V, g, β, cu_seqlens
│
├── cumsum       prefix cumulative sum of gate logits g        [Vec]
├── kkt          intra-chunk K^T K attention matrix A          [Cube+Vec]
├── solve_tril   lower-triangular solve A_inv = tril(A)^{-1}  [CubeCore]
├── wy_fast      Woodbury updates W, U from K, V, β, A_inv    [Vec+Cube]
├── chunk_h      inter-chunk recurrent state S and V'          [Cube+Vec]
└── chunk_o      output O = Q (K^T V' + S)                    [Cube+Vec]
```

GQA is fully supported: Q/K use `Hg` heads while V/gates use `H ≥ Hg` value
heads.

---

## Changes

### New: `csrc/pto_chunk_gdn/`

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `mega_kernel.cpp` | Fused megakernel entry point (all six stages) |
| `chunk_cumsum.cpp` | Cumulative sum stage (included by mega_kernel.cpp) |
| `scaled_dot_kkt.cpp` | K^T K attention matrix (included by mega_kernel.cpp) |
| `tri_inverse_impl.cpp` | Triangular inverse implementation (included by mega_kernel.cpp) |
| `wy_fast.cpp` | Woodbury W/U updates (included by mega_kernel.cpp) |
| `chunk_h.cpp` | Inter-chunk recurrent state (included by mega_kernel.cpp) |
| `chunk_o.cpp` | Output projection (included by mega_kernel.cpp) |
| `include/kernel_utils.h` | Shared AI-Core utility templates |
| `CMakeLists.txt` | Optional `BUILD_PTO_CHUNK_GDN` target for pre-compilation |

### New: `csrc/third_party/pto-isa` (git submodule)

PTO ISA header library required by the megakernel.  Added at the same level
as the existing `catlass` submodule:
```
csrc/third_party/pto-isa   ← new  (gitcode.com/cann/pto-isa.git)
csrc/third_party/catlass    ← existing
```

### New: `vllm_ascend/ops/pto_chunk_gdn/`

| Module | Description |
|---|---|
| `compile.py` | Bisheng JIT compilation; resolves `PTO_LIB_PATH`; caches `.so` |
| `mega_kernel.py` | ctypes launcher for the fused megakernel |
| `chunk_gated_delta_wrapper.py` | Drop-in `chunk_gated_delta_rule` replacement; handles GQA and Triton fallback for decode |
| `worker_hook.py` | `apply_pto_gdn_patch()` — patches `chunk_gated_delta_rule` at worker startup |

### Modified: `vllm_ascend/envs.py`

One new environment variable:

```python
VLLM_ASCEND_PTO_CHUNK_GDN   # bool, default False; enable PTO megakernel
```

### Modified: `vllm_ascend/patch/worker/__init__.py`

Native activation hook — runs after Triton patches, before model loading:

```python
if not is_310p():
    if envs.VLLM_ASCEND_PTO_CHUNK_GDN:
        from vllm_ascend.ops.pto_chunk_gdn.worker_hook import apply_pto_gdn_patch
        apply_pto_gdn_patch()
```

### Modified: `vllm_ascend/ops/gdn.py`

Changed static import to module-level attribute access so the worker hook
patch applies correctly:

```python
# Before
from vllm_ascend.ops.triton.fla.chunk import chunk_gated_delta_rule

# After
import vllm_ascend.ops.triton.fla.chunk as _fla_chunk_mod
# ...
(out, state) = _fla_chunk_mod.chunk_gated_delta_rule(...)
```

### New: `docs/source/user_guide/feature_guide/enable_megagdn_kernel.md`

Complete user guide covering quick-start, performance benchmarks, lm-eval
accuracy verification (with commands), CMake pre-compilation, and
troubleshooting.

---

## Performance Results

Measured on Ascend 910B4 with Qwen3.5-0.8B (BF16, eager mode, single device,
**rebuilt from source using this PR**):

| Backend | 512 tok TTFT | 1024 tok TTFT | 4096 tok TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|
| Triton (default)  | 125.8 ms | 125.3 ms | 133.8 ms |
| PTO megakernel    | 110.6 ms | 111.7 ms | 119.9 ms |
| **Speedup**       | **1.14×** | **1.12×** | **1.12×** |

For larger models (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MoE) where GDN layers dominate, speedups
reach **~25% at 4k+ tokens**.

---

## Accuracy Results (Qwen3.5-0.8B)

256-document wikitext subset + 6-subject MMLU
(**rebuilt from source using this PR**):

| Backend | WikiText PPL ↓ | MMLU acc ↑ |
|---|---|---|
| Triton (default) | 20.93 | 48.9% |
| PTO megakernel   | 20.93 | 48.9% |

Zero accuracy difference.

---

## Testing

```bash
# E2E inference: PTO and Triton produce identical outputs
ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
VLLM_ASCEND_PTO_CHUNK_GDN=1 \
python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
    --model /path/to/Qwen3.5-0.8B --max-model-len 1024

# lm-eval accuracy
ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
VLLM_ASCEND_PTO_CHUNK_GDN=1 \
python -m lm_eval --model vllm \
    --model_args "pretrained=/path/to/Qwen3.5-0.8B" \
    --tasks wikitext --limit 256
```

---

## Limitations

- Single-device only (TP=1, EP=1).  Multi-device support will be addressed in follow-up PRs.
- Chunk size fixed at C=128 (optimal tiling for Ascend 910B AI-Core).
- 910C/A3 uses the same code path but is not tested in the current CI environment.

---

## Notes for Reviewers

- Fully in-tree: no external dependencies beyond the `csrc/third_party/pto-isa` git submodule.
- `VLLM_ASCEND_PTO_CHUNK_GDN` is registered in `vllm_ascend/envs.py`; the
  "Unknown vLLM environment variable" warning from vLLM core is harmless.
- The JIT cache directory (`kernels/compiled_lib/*.so`) is listed in `.gitignore`.

---

## How to Rebuild from Source

### Prerequisites

- Ascend 910B device with CANN ≥ 8.0 and `bisheng` compiler in `PATH`
- Ubuntu 22.04 (recommended) with Python 3.11
- Activate the toolkit: `source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh`

### Build steps

```bash
# 1 — Clone with submodules
git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend.git
cd vllm-ascend
git submodule update --init --recursive   # pulls pto-isa and catlass

# 2 — Install vLLM (empty device build — no GPU/CUDA needed)
git clone --depth 1 -b v0.19.1 https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git /tmp/vllm
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty pip install -e /tmp/vllm/ \
    --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu/
pip uninstall -y triton

# 3 — Install vllm-ascend
pip install -e . \
    --extra-index-url https://mirrors.huaweicloud.com/ascend/repos/pypi \
    --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu/
pip uninstall -y triton triton-ascend
pip install triton-ascend==3.2.0

# 4 — (Optional) Pre-compile PTO megakernel for common Qwen configs
cmake -S csrc -B csrc/build -DBUILD_PTO_CHUNK_GDN=ON
cmake --build csrc/build --target pto_chunk_gdn_kernels -j$(nproc)
```

### Run inference with PTO

```bash
ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
VLLM_ASCEND_PTO_CHUNK_GDN=1 \
python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
    --model /path/to/Qwen3.5-7B \
    --max-model-len 8192
```

### Run accuracy check (lm-eval)

```bash
pip install lm-eval sacrebleu more-itertools datasets

# Triton baseline
ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m lm_eval \
    --model vllm \
    --model_args "pretrained=/path/to/Qwen3.5-0.8B,gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,enforce_eager=True" \
    --tasks "wikitext" --limit 256 --output_path results/triton.json

# PTO megakernel
ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_ASCEND_PTO_CHUNK_GDN=1 python -m lm_eval \
    --model vllm \
    --model_args "pretrained=/path/to/Qwen3.5-0.8B,gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,enforce_eager=True" \
    --tasks "wikitext" --limit 256 --output_path results/pto.json
```

---

## Minimum Dockerfile

A minimum `Dockerfile.pto` is included at the repository root for building a
self-contained image with CANN 8.5.1, vLLM v0.19.1, and vllm-ascend with PTO
pre-compiled for common Qwen configurations.

```dockerfile
FROM quay.io/ascend/cann:8.5.1-910b-ubuntu22.04-py3.11

ARG PIP_INDEX_URL="https://pypi.org/simple"
ARG VLLM_REPO="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git"
ARG VLLM_TAG="v0.19.1"
ARG SOC_VERSION="ascend910b4"

WORKDIR /workspace

# System packages
RUN apt-get update -y && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        git cmake ninja-build gcc g++ wget numactl libnuma-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN pip config set global.index-url ${PIP_INDEX_URL}

# vLLM (empty-device build)
RUN git clone --depth 1 -b ${VLLM_TAG} ${VLLM_REPO} /workspace/vllm && \
    VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE="empty" pip install -v -e /workspace/vllm/ \
        --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu/ && \
    pip uninstall -y triton && pip cache purge

# vllm-ascend with pto-isa submodule
COPY . /workspace/vllm-ascend/
RUN cd /workspace/vllm-ascend && \
    git submodule update --init --recursive csrc/third_party/pto-isa

ENV SOC_VERSION=${SOC_VERSION} TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1

RUN source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh && \
    source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh 2>/dev/null || true && \
    export PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL=https://mirrors.huaweicloud.com/ascend/repos/pypi && \
    pip install -v -e /workspace/vllm-ascend/ \
        --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu/ && \
    pip uninstall -y triton triton-ascend 2>/dev/null || true && \
    pip install -v triton-ascend==3.2.0 && pip cache purge

# Pre-compile PTO megakernel (optional — remove to rely on JIT)
RUN source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh && \
    cmake -S /workspace/vllm-ascend/csrc \
          -B /workspace/vllm-ascend/csrc/build \
          -DBUILD_PTO_CHUNK_GDN=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && \
    cmake --build /workspace/vllm-ascend/csrc/build \
          --target pto_chunk_gdn_kernels -j$(nproc) && \
    rm -rf /workspace/vllm-ascend/csrc/build

ENV VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn \
    VLLM_ASCEND_PTO_CHUNK_GDN=1

RUN echo "source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh" >> ~/.bashrc

CMD ["/bin/bash"]
```

Build and run:

```bash
# Build image (from vllm-ascend repo root)
docker build --build-arg SOC_VERSION=ascend910b4 \
    -t vllm-ascend-pto:latest -f Dockerfile.pto .

# Run inference
docker run --rm -it \
    --device /dev/davinci0 --device /dev/davinci_manager \
    --device /dev/devmm_svm --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
    -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
    -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64 \
    -v /path/to/model:/model \
    vllm-ascend-pto:latest \
    python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
        --model /model --max-model-len 8192
```

- vLLM version: v0.19.1

items.title: [Test][Triton] Add single-kernel KDA coverage
items.body:
## What this PR does / why we need it

This is a follow-up to #9035, which introduced the KDA Triton operators for Ascend NPU with operator-level end-to-end coverage.

This PR adds direct NPU precision tests for all 16 production KDA Triton kernels and a KDA operator description following the Triton documentation specification. Each test function:

- directly raw-launches exactly one target `kernel[grid](...)`;
- compares its outputs with an independent PyTorch CPU FP32 reference;
- avoids calling production wrappers or chaining multiple production kernels.

Only tests and operator documentation are changed. There is no production-code or user-facing behavior change.

## Coverage

- Auxiliary kernels: scalar/vector chunk cumsum, persistent/tiled L2Norm, 16x16 triangular solve, and 32x32/64x64 inverse merge.
- Core kernels: two gated LayerNorm variants, two scaled KKT variants, W/U recomputation, chunk output, and KDA gate.
- State kernels: chunk-state propagation and fused recurrent KDA.

The 25 collected cases cover FP32/FP16/BF16, fixed and variable-length layouts, partial tail chunks, non-power-of-two dimensions, optional inputs, and in-place/non-in-place state paths.

## Documentation

- Added `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/kda.md` using the structure defined by `triton_description_specification.md`.
- Documented the KDA recurrence, the 16-kernel chunk/recurrent execution flow, public parameters and tensor layouts, constraints, upstream origin and Ascend-specific differences, and the single-kernel validation results.
- Renamed the three new test files to remove the `_npu` suffix; no test logic changed during the rename.

## Single-kernel test methodology

The tests deliberately validate the raw Triton kernels instead of the composed KDA operators:

1. Each test function targets one imported production `@triton.jit` kernel and manually prepares its input/output tensors, launch grid, constexpr metadata, and variable-length metadata (`cu_seqlens`, `chunk_indices`, or `chunk_offsets`) when required.
2. The function directly calls the target `kernel[grid](...)` exactly once and synchronizes the NPU. It does not call a production wrapper and does not launch another production kernel to prepare inputs or post-process outputs.
3. Expected outputs are calculated independently on CPU in FP32 from the actual quantized kernel inputs. The references use PyTorch tensor operations or explicit recurrent/block-matrix equations and do not reuse KDA production helpers.
4. Non-finite outputs are rejected and numerical results are compared with `torch.testing.assert_close`. Tolerances are selected by the numerical behavior of each kernel family:
   - cumsum: `rtol=1e-5`, `atol=1e-5`;
   - L2Norm: `rtol=3e-4`, `atol=1e-3`;
   - triangular solve/inverse merge: `rtol=5e-4`, `atol=5e-4`;
   - gated LayerNorm statistics: `rtol=8e-4`, `atol=8e-4`;
   - low-precision matrix/recurrent kernels: FP16/BF16 tolerances from `1e-2` up to `6e-2`, depending on the accumulated path.
5. An AST audit checks that all 16 test functions contain exactly one raw production-kernel launch, preserving a one-test-to-one-kernel mapping even for parameterized cases.

The inputs exercise fixed and flattened variable-length batches, aligned and partial chunks, head mapping, non-power-of-two dimensions, optional residual/weight/bias paths, both activation variants, scalar/vector beta, and in-place/non-in-place state updates.

## How was this patch tested?

- Ascend A3 full single-kernel suite:

  | Test file | Kernels | Collected cases | Result |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | `test_kda_aux_kernels.py` | 7 | 7 | 7 passed |
  | `test_kda_core_kernels.py` | 7 | 14 | 14 passed |
  | `test_kda_state_kernels.py` | 2 | 4 | 4 passed |
  | **Total** | **16** | **25** | **25 passed, 0 failed** |

  The final complete run finished in 23.24 seconds with the Triton compilation cache warm.

- `python3 -m py_compile` on all three new test files
- `ruff check` on all three new test files
- `ruff format --check` on all three new test files
- `markdownlint` on `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/kda.md`
- AST audit confirming one raw production-kernel launch per test function

items.title: [Feature] Support Bailing V3 on Ascend NPU
items.body:
## Overview

This PR adds support for **Bailing V3** (a hybrid MoE model with Kimi Delta Attention) on Ascend NPU, and includes a quick-deployment patch mechanism for the existing v0.20.2 release image.

Since the corresponding upstream vLLM changes are merged into `main` rather than the `v0.20.2` release branch, this PR ships both the feature code and a set of pre-built patches so that users of the v0.20.2 image can try Bailing V3 without building from source.

## What's Included

### 1. Bailing V3 Feature Support (commit `b8a822c6`)

The following capabilities are introduced:

- **KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) Triton Kernels**: New Ascend NPU Triton kernels under `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/kda/`, including both chunk-based and fused-recurrent implementations. These provide the linear-attention component of Bailing V3's hybrid architecture.
- **Gated Attention in MLA**: Enhanced `AscendMultiHeadLatentAttention` to support the gated projection (`g_proj`) with head-wise and element-wise granularity, as well as the `skip_o_proj` path used by Bailing V3.
- **Mamba/SSM KV-Cache Config**: Updated `MambaModelConfig` to handle KDA models that carry multiple CONV states (3x) alongside an SSM state, with proper padding alignment on Ascend hardware.
- **MTP (Multi-Token Prediction)**: Speculative decoding support for Bailing V3 via MTP, including `bailing_hybrid_v3_mtp` model type registration, speculative config overrides, and `lm_head` weight-sharing logic in the MTP proposer.
- **ModelSlim Quantization**: Updated quantization prefix mapping to correctly handle Bailing V3 MTP shared-head weights.
- **GDN Attention Backend**: Adjustments to the Gated Delta Network attention backend for Bailing V3 compatibility.

Key files changed:

- `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/kda/` — new KDA Triton kernels (chunk, fused recurrent, cumsum, l2norm, solve_tril, etc.)
- `vllm_ascend/ops/bailing_moe_v3_kda.py` — Bailing V3 KDA ops integration
- `vllm_ascend/ops/mla.py`, `vllm_ascend/attention/mla_v1.py` — gated attention & skip o_proj support
- `vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_mamba_config.py` — KDA SSM/CONV cache layout
- `vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_speculative_config.py` — Bailing V3 MTP registration
- `vllm_ascend/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py` — MTP lm_head sharing
- `vllm_ascend/quantization/modelslim_config.py` — quantization prefix mapping

Both `vllm` and `vllm-ascend` require changes. The vLLM-side changes include the Bailing V3 model definition (`bailing_moe_v3.py`, `bailing_moe_v3_mtp.py`), KDA layer ops fixes, speculative config, and model registry updates.

### 2. Quick Deployment Patches

A patch script and pre-generated git patches are added under `docs/bailing_v3_adpater/`:

- `patch_bailing_v3.sh` — one-click script to apply/revert patches
- `bailing_v3_vllm.patch` — patch for vLLM
- `bailing_v3_vllm_ascend.patch` — patch for vllm-ascend

## Quick Start: Try Bailing V3 on the v0.20.2 Image

If you are already running the v0.20.2 release image (e.g. `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.20.2rc1`), you can enable Bailing V3 support without rebuilding:

### Step 1: Pull and start the v0.20.2 image

```bash
# Atlas A3: quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:nightly-releases-v0.20.2rc-a3-openeuler
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:nightly-releases-v0.20.2rc-a3-openeuler
docker run --rm \
    --name vllm-ascend \
    --shm-size=1g \
    --net=host \
    --device /dev/davinci0 \
    --device /dev/davinci1 \
    --device /dev/davinci2 \
    --device /dev/davinci3 \

    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool \
    -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \

    -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
    -v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \

```

### Step 2: Clone this branch or download the attatched，and run the patch script
[bailing_v3_adpater.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30741268/bailing_v3_adpater.zip)
```bash

cd /workspace/vllm-ascend/docs/bailing_v3_adpater
```

The script will automatically:

1. Locate the installed `vllm` and `vllm-ascend` packages in the current Python environment.


### Reverting patches

To cleanly revert the patches (e.g. before switching models):

```bash
bash patch_bailing_v3.sh --reverse
```

## Notes

- The patches are generated against the v0.20.2 release. They may not apply cleanly on other versions.
- KDA Triton kernels require Triton with Ascend NPU support (already included in the v0.20.2 image).

items.title: [BugFix] chunk_gated_delta_rule MTE out-of-bounds and test validity
items.body:
## Problem

The `chunk_gated_delta_rule` AscendC operator crashes with `AICore MTE out-of-bounds` (error 507015, MPU address access invalid) when called with `cu_seqlens` but without `prebuilt_meta`. This happens because `chunk_indices_chunk64` is left as `None`, and the `chunk_fwd_o` kernel reads `gmChunkOffsets` from nullptr when `isVariedLen=true`.

Additionally, the existing test `test_triton_fusion_ops` has multiple issues that mask the crash:

1. **cu_seqlens/seqlen mismatch**: `cu_seqlens=[0,1,2,3]` with `seqlen=17` — only 1 token per sequence is allocated, but the kernel reads 64 tokens per chunk.
2. **Invalid gate values**: `g` uses `randn` (positive values cause `exp(g)` to explode); `beta` uses `randn` (should be in [0,1]).
3. **No numerical check**: Only shape assertions, which silently pass even when the kernel crashes (NPU execution is asynchronous).

## Fix

### `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/fla/chunk.py`
Auto-generate `chunk_indices_chunk64` via `prepare_chunk_indices(cu_seqlens, chunk_size)` when `prebuilt_meta is None` but `cu_seqlens` is provided. Also guard `cu_seqlens.to(torch.int64)` against `None`.

### `tests/.../test_chunk_gated_delta_rule.py`
- Use `logsigmoid` for `g` and `sigmoid` for `beta` (physically valid ranges).
- Use `cu_seqlens=[0, 64, 128, 192]` with `seqlen=192` (3 sequences of 64 tokens each, matching chunk_size).
- Add numerical correctness check against the fp32 PyTorch reference (`rtol=5e-2, atol=5e-2` to accommodate bf16 vs fp32 divergence).
- Use `SimpleNamespace` for `mock_pcp_group` to ensure `world_size` comparison works correctly.

| Module | Description |
|---|---|
| `compile.py` | Bisheng JIT compilation; resolves `PTO_LIB_PATH`; caches `.so` |
| `mega_kernel.py` | ctypes launcher for the fused megakernel |
| `chunk_gated_delta_wrapper.py` | Drop-in `chunk_gated_delta_rule` replacement; handles GQA and Triton fallback for decode |
| `worker_hook.py` | `apply_pto_gdn_patch()` — patches `chunk_gated_delta_rule` at worker startup |

### Modified: `vllm_ascend/envs.py`

One new environment variable:

```python
VLLM_ASCEND_PTO_CHUNK_GDN   # bool, default False; enable PTO megakernel
```

### Modified: `vllm_ascend/patch/worker/__init__.py`

Native activation hook — runs after Triton patches, before model loading:

```python
if not is_310p():
    if envs.VLLM_ASCEND_PTO_CHUNK_GDN:
        from vllm_ascend.ops.pto_chunk_gdn.worker_hook import apply_pto_gdn_patch
        apply_pto_gdn_patch()
```

### Modified: `vllm_ascend/ops/gdn.py`

Changed static import to module-level attribute access so the worker hook
patch applies correctly:

```python
# Before
from vllm_ascend.ops.triton.fla.chunk import chunk_gated_delta_rule

# After
import vllm_ascend.ops.triton.fla.chunk as _fla_chunk_mod
# ...
(out, state) = _fla_chunk_mod.chunk_gated_delta_rule(...)
```

### New: `docs/source/user_guide/feature_guide/enable_megagdn_kernel.md`

Complete user guide covering quick-start, performance benchmarks, lm-eval
accuracy verification (with commands), CMake pre-compilation, and
troubleshooting.

---

## Performance Results

Measured on Ascend 910B4 with Qwen3.5-0.8B (BF16, eager mode, single device,
**rebuilt from source using this PR**):

| Backend | 512 tok TTFT | 1024 tok TTFT | 4096 tok TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|
| Triton (default)  | 125.8 ms | 125.3 ms | 133.8 ms |
| PTO megakernel    | 110.6 ms | 111.7 ms | 119.9 ms |
| **Speedup**       | **1.14×** | **1.12×** | **1.12×** |

For larger models (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MoE) where GDN layers dominate, speedups
reach **~25% at 4k+ tokens**.

---

## Accuracy Results (Qwen3.5-0.8B)

256-document wikitext subset + 6-subject MMLU
(**rebuilt from source using this PR**):

| Backend | WikiText PPL ↓ | MMLU acc ↑ |
|---|---|---|
| Triton (default) | 20.93 | 48.9% |
| PTO megakernel   | 20.93 | 48.9% |

Zero accuracy difference.

---

## Testing

```bash
# E2E inference: PTO and Triton produce identical outputs
ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
VLLM_ASCEND_PTO_CHUNK_GDN=1 \
python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
    --model /path/to/Qwen3.5-0.8B --max-model-len 1024

# lm-eval accuracy
ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
VLLM_ASCEND_PTO_CHUNK_GDN=1 \
python -m lm_eval --model vllm \
    --model_args "pretrained=/path/to/Qwen3.5-0.8B" \
    --tasks wikitext --limit 256
```

---

## Limitations

- Single-device only (TP=1, EP=1).  Multi-device support will be addressed in follow-up PRs.
- Chunk size fixed at C=128 (optimal tiling for Ascend 910B AI-Core).
- 910C/A3 uses the same code path but is not tested in the current CI environment.

---

## Notes for Reviewers

- Fully in-tree: no external dependencies beyond the `csrc/third_party/pto-isa` git submodule.
- `VLLM_ASCEND_PTO_CHUNK_GDN` is registered in `vllm_ascend/envs.py`; the
  "Unknown vLLM environment variable" warning from vLLM core is harmless.
- The JIT cache directory (`kernels/compiled_lib/*.so`) is listed in `.gitignore`.

---

## How to Rebuild from Source

### Prerequisites

- Ascend 910B device with CANN ≥ 8.0 and `bisheng` compiler in `PATH`
- Ubuntu 22.04 (recommended) with Python 3.11
- Activate the toolkit: `source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh`

### Build steps

```bash
# 1 — Clone with submodules
git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend.git
cd vllm-ascend
git submodule update --init --recursive   # pulls pto-isa and catlass

# 2 — Install vLLM (empty device build — no GPU/CUDA needed)
git clone --depth 1 -b v0.19.1 https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git /tmp/vllm
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty pip install -e /tmp/vllm/ \
    --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu/
pip uninstall -y triton

# 3 — Install vllm-ascend
pip install -e . \
    --extra-index-url https://mirrors.huaweicloud.com/ascend/repos/pypi \
    --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu/
pip uninstall -y triton triton-ascend
pip install triton-ascend==3.2.0

# 4 — (Optional) Pre-compile PTO megakernel for common Qwen configs
cmake -S csrc -B csrc/build -DBUILD_PTO_CHUNK_GDN=ON
cmake --build csrc/build --target pto_chunk_gdn_kernels -j$(nproc)
```

### Run inference with PTO

```bash
ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
VLLM_ASCEND_PTO_CHUNK_GDN=1 \
python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
    --model /path/to/Qwen3.5-7B \
    --max-model-len 8192
```

### Run accuracy check (lm-eval)

```bash
pip install lm-eval sacrebleu more-itertools datasets

# Triton baseline
ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m lm_eval \
    --model vllm \
    --model_args "pretrained=/path/to/Qwen3.5-0.8B,gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,enforce_eager=True" \
    --tasks "wikitext" --limit 256 --output_path results/triton.json

# PTO megakernel
ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_ASCEND_PTO_CHUNK_GDN=1 python -m lm_eval \
    --model vllm \
    --model_args "pretrained=/path/to/Qwen3.5-0.8B,gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,enforce_eager=True" \
    --tasks "wikitext" --limit 256 --output_path results/pto.json
```

---

## Minimum Dockerfile

A minimum `Dockerfile.pto` is included at the repository root for building a
self-contained image with CANN 8.5.1, vLLM v0.19.1, and vllm-ascend with PTO
pre-compiled for common Qwen configurations.

```dockerfile
FROM quay.io/ascend/cann:8.5.1-910b-ubuntu22.04-py3.11

ARG PIP_INDEX_URL="https://pypi.org/simple"
ARG VLLM_REPO="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git"
ARG VLLM_TAG="v0.19.1"
ARG SOC_VERSION="ascend910b4"

WORKDIR /workspace

# System packages
RUN apt-get update -y && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        git cmake ninja-build gcc g++ wget numactl libnuma-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN pip config set global.index-url ${PIP_INDEX_URL}

# vLLM (empty-device build)
RUN git clone --depth 1 -b ${VLLM_TAG} ${VLLM_REPO} /workspace/vllm && \
    VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE="empty" pip install -v -e /workspace/vllm/ \
        --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu/ && \
    pip uninstall -y triton && pip cache purge

# vllm-ascend with pto-isa submodule
COPY . /workspace/vllm-ascend/
RUN cd /workspace/vllm-ascend && \
    git submodule update --init --recursive csrc/third_party/pto-isa

ENV SOC_VERSION=${SOC_VERSION} TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1

RUN source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh && \
    source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh 2>/dev/null || true && \
    export PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL=https://mirrors.huaweicloud.com/ascend/repos/pypi && \
    pip install -v -e /workspace/vllm-ascend/ \
        --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu/ && \
    pip uninstall -y triton triton-ascend 2>/dev/null || true && \
    pip install -v triton-ascend==3.2.0 && pip cache purge

# Pre-compile PTO megakernel (optional — remove to rely on JIT)
RUN source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh && \
    cmake -S /workspace/vllm-ascend/csrc \
          -B /workspace/vllm-ascend/csrc/build \
          -DBUILD_PTO_CHUNK_GDN=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && \
    cmake --build /workspace/vllm-ascend/csrc/build \
          --target pto_chunk_gdn_kernels -j$(nproc) && \
    rm -rf /workspace/vllm-ascend/csrc/build

ENV VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn \
    VLLM_ASCEND_PTO_CHUNK_GDN=1

RUN echo "source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh" >> ~/.bashrc

CMD ["/bin/bash"]
```

Build and run:

```bash
# Build image (from vllm-ascend repo root)
docker build --build-arg SOC_VERSION=ascend910b4 \
    -t vllm-ascend-pto:latest -f Dockerfile.pto .

# Run inference
docker run --rm -it \
    --device /dev/davinci0 --device /dev/davinci_manager \
    --device /dev/devmm_svm --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
    -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
    -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64 \
    -v /path/to/model:/model \
    vllm-ascend-pto:latest \
    python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
        --model /model --max-model-len 8192
```

- vLLM version: v0.19.1
- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/d886c26d4d4fef7d079696beb4ece1cfb4b008a8

items.title: [Ascend950] [Feature] Support custom op for GDN on Ascend 950
items.body:
[Ascend950] [Feature] Support custom op for GDN on Ascend 950

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR enables custom operator support for **Gated Delta Network (GDN)** on Ascend 950 (A5), and fixes several compilation issues introduced by previous platform filtering logic.

**Background & Motivation**
- PR [#9271](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/9271) excluded ATB-based kernels (e.g., `get_masked_input_and_mask`, `bgmv_expand`, `sgmv_expand`) from Ascend 950 via the compile macro `VLLM_ENABLE_ATB_AND_DIRECT_KERNELS`. However, the exclusion logic in `vllm_ascend/meta_registration.py` was incomplete: when `get_ascend_device_type() == AscendDeviceType.A5`, the code still attempted to register meta kernels for these ATB-only ops via `register_meta_if_necessary`, causing **compilation errors** on 950.
- Additionally, the existing custom op build pipeline (`build_aclnn.sh`) did not correctly aggregate `binary_info_config.json` for A5-specific kernels, and some AscendC host tiling code (`recurrent_gated_delta_rule_tiling_arch35.cpp`) had C++ access-control issues when compiled under the unified `ophost_transformer_tiling_obj` target.

**Changes Made**
1. **Fix 950 compilation guard in `meta_registration.py`**
   - Skip `register_meta_if_necessary` for ATB-only ops (`get_masked_input_and_mask`, `bgmv_expand`, `sgmv_expand`, etc.) on A5, aligning with the `VLLM_ENABLE_ATB_AND_DIRECT_KERNELS` macro.

2. **Add A5-compatible custom AscendC kernels**
   - `causal_conv1d`
   - `recurrent_gated_delta_rule`
   - `chunk_fwd_o`
   - `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h`
   - These kernels are registered under the `arch35` host tiling path for Ascend 950 and properly packaged into `vllm_ascend/_cann_ops_custom`.

3. **Fix custom Triton kernel bugs on Ascend 950**
   - `chunk_scaled_dot_kkt`
   - `solve_tril`

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. All changes are backend compilation and operator registration fixes. No Python API or CLI behavior is changed.

### How was this PR tested?

**Environment**

**Ascend 950 (A5)**
- Model: Qwen3-Next
- GSM8K accuracy:
  - `W8A8_MXFP` (MXFP8): **96.44**, **96.36**
  - `BF16`: **96.13**, **96.44**

**Ascend 910B**
- Model: Qwen3-Next
- GSM8K accuracy:
  - `BF16`: **95.83**, **96.21**

labels.name: ready-precise

items.body: ### What this PR does / why we need it? `_forward_core`'s prepare stage runs on every GDN layer of every step and used to issue the whole legacy chain below, once per token subset (spec batches have two subsets): **Legacy prepare chain (what this PR replaces):** | # | Legacy step | What it did | Device cost | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | `rearrange_mixed_qkv(mixed_qkv)` | `torch.split` the packed `[T, qkv_dim]` row into q/k/v sections, then reshape each section to `[1, T, heads, dim]` + `.contiguous()` | 3 contiguous-copy kernels + host dispatches | | 2 | `l2norm_fwd(query)` | L2-normalize q over the head dim (fp32 accumulation) | 1 triton launch + autotune host overhead | | 3 | `l2norm_fwd(key)` | same for k | 1 triton launch + autotune host overhead | | 4 | `DeviceOperator.fused_gdn_gating(A_log, a, b, dt_bias)` | `g = -exp(A_log) * softplus(a + dt_bias)` (fp32, beta=1, threshold=20), `beta = sigmoid(b)` | 1 triton launch | | 5 | spec/mixed batches only: `g/beta.index_select(1, token_indx)` × 4 | select the g/beta rows of each token subset | 4 gather kernels | This PR replaces the entire chain with **one** Triton kernel, `fused_gdn_prepare`, which: - reads `mixed_qkv` **in place** through the section offsets (q at 0, k at `key_dim/tp`, v at `2*key_dim/tp` inside each packed row) — no host-side split/copy; - L2-normalizes q/k over the head dim with fp32 accumulation (`x * rsqrt(sum(x^2) + 1e-6)`), byte-for-byte the semantics of `l2norm_fwd`; - streams v through to a contiguous `[1, T, Nv, Dv]` output; - computes the gating (`g`, `beta`) per token, identical to `fused_gdn_gating`; - on the spec path (`HAS_INDEX` variant) also gathers the a/b rows **inline** via the token index map (indirect addressing), folding the four `index_select` dispatches into the same launch — gating is token-wise, so per-subset gating equals full-batch gating (the pure-spec case builds `spec_token_indx` as `arange`, so the gather is an identity there too). Outputs follow the legacy batched convention (`[1, T, Nk, Dk]` / `[1, T, Nv, Dv]` / `[1, T, Nv]`), so the downstream is shape-identical and the eager prefill path needs zero shape ops. **Downstream adjustments enabled by pre-normalized q/k:** - decode (no spec): 1 launch replaces rearrange + 2x l2norm + gating; - prefill (no spec): all three prefill paths skip the now-redundant q/k normalization — the fla path stops issuing its two `l2norm_fwd` dispatches (Base adaptor) or the in-kernel normalization (A5 adaptor) via the new `qk_pre_normalized` flag, the fused CANN path gets the same flag, and the Triton pipeline gets `use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=False`; - spec/mixed batches: the kernel runs once per conv output subset with the index-gather variant; - launch path: the `CompiledKernel` is cached per (config, `BLOCK_T` tier, dtypes) — `T`/`NUM_CHUNKS` are `do_not_specialize` runtime args and the grid is recomputed per call, so one binary per tier serves every token count and the >100us `JITFunction` dispatch is bypassed on every call after the first per tier (~30-40us via `ck.run`, kernel itself ~40us); `BLOCK_T` tiers are precompiled on first use and the standard launch path is kept as fallback. The integration reaches the runtime class through method patching (`patch/worker/patch_qwen3_5.py`); the flag is resolved defensively in `_forward_core` so any class that picked up the patched method without the fused attrs falls back to the legacy chain (flip `_use_fused_gdn_prepare` to False to restore it). ### GDN Prepare Stage: Fused Triton Kernel Analysis #### Prefill Path (per GDN layer, T=4106 tokens) **Without fused kernel (main baseline):** | # | Kernel | Type | Duration (µs) | |---|--------|------|----------| | 1 | `Slice` (split q) | AI_VECTOR_CORE | 6.7 | | 2 | `Slice` (split k) | AI_VECTOR_CORE | 6.4 | | 3 | `Slice` (split v) | AI_VECTOR_CORE | 8.7 | | 4 | `ConcatD` (reshape v) | AI_VECTOR_CORE | 17.5 | | 5 | `fused_gdn_gating` | AI_VECTOR_CORE | 20.3 | | 6 | `_clear_ssm_states` | AI_VECTOR_CORE | 6.0 | | 7 | `l2norm_fwd` (q) | AI_VECTOR_CORE | 15.4 | | 8 | `l2norm_fwd` (k) | AI_VECTOR_CORE | 10.1 | | | **Prepare subtotal** | | **84.7 µs** | | | *(+ `ChunkGatedDeltaRule` 894 µs)* | | | **Before (legacy prepare chain: rearrange copies + 2x l2norm + gating + index_selects):** **With fused kernel (this PR):** | # items.title: [Performance][GDN] Cut host dispatch on the GDN prefill path
items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Prefill steps on the GDN path run eagerly, so the number of host-side launches
sets how long the device sits idle. `_forward_core` was doing per-layer host work
that a single fused launch can cover.

Three changes, all guarded on `spec_sequence_masks is None`, `num_prefills > 0`
and `pcp world_size == 1`. Pure decode replays a graph and is untouched; the
`pcp > 1` branch is untouched.

1. **q and k are l2-normalised in one Triton launch instead of two.**
   `rearrange_mixed_qkv` packs q, k and v back to back into one buffer, so q and k
   are adjacent contiguous views of a single storage and can be normalised as one
   `(2N, D)` tensor. Each `l2norm_fwd` launch costs ~220 us of host Python
   whatever the row count. Guarded on same storage, adjacent offset and
   contiguity; falls back to two calls and logs a warning if that layout ever
   changes.
2. **The decode segment of a mixed batch is sliced out of the already-normalised
   batch** instead of being re-packed by a second `rearrange_mixed_qkv` and
   re-normalised. Saves a split, three reshape copies, a cat and two l2norm
   launches per layer.
3. **`clear_ssm_states` (a Triton wrapper) becomes `masked_fill_`**, two aten ops.

### Does this PR introduce *any* user-facing change?

No. The output is bit-exact against the previous path, not merely close.

### How was this patch tested?

Measured on A2 (910B4 x4), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B TP4+EP.

- Host time per mixed step per GDN layer: **1895 -> 862 us**.
- Eight-session A/B, exact permutation test over session means (the session is the
  unit of variance; burst-level p-values overstate): burst 32x4096 in / 32 out
  **6.116 -> 5.993 s (-2.01%, p=0.057)**; median TTFT **3042 -> 2978 ms
  (-2.12%, p=0.029**, the two arms do not overlap). Decode-dominated full bench is
  -1.0% and not significant, as expected.

Bit-exactness:

- 61 single-card shape cases identical bit for bit.
- `masked_fill_` identical to `clear_ssm_states`.
- The aclnn chunk op accepts the offset views.
- With `HCCL_DETERMINISTIC=true`, the serving fingerprint (top-20 logprobs of the
  first generated token, 3k/9k/17k-token prompts, pure prefill and mixed with live
  decoders) is **12/12 identical** to base — which is also what base-vs-base gives.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

items.title: [Performance][KDA] Overlap Conv1d metadata slicing
items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The KDA Conv1d path currently materializes the final cache-index row slice on the main stream immediately before Conv1d. The profiler shows this short Slice directly in the QKV-to-Conv1d critical path.

This patch gives KDA a dedicated metadata builder/backend pair that leaves the source cache-index tensor unsliced. After the long BFG projection is submitted, KDA enqueues the required row slices on a separate vector stream and records one completion event. The main stream waits for that event immediately before Conv1d. Speculative, prefill, and decode metadata are all covered; generic GDN keeps its existing builder behavior.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This is an internal KDA Ascend stream scheduling optimization.

items.title: [Performance][Spec Decode] Capture GLM MTP metadata and avoid padding stalls
items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

A captured GLM MTP draft model still performs input/metadata work outside the graph. Later draft steps also used the first verify-token bucket even though they only need one row per request. Separately, GDN's padding metadata uploaded a tiny corrected CPU boundary tensor synchronously, delaying selected ranks before the next target graph and making their EP peers wait inside MoE Dispatch.

This PR:
- Keeps the first verify-sized draft forward and uses request-sized capacity for later steps, including MC2 padding.
- Captures later-step metadata updates with the model; uses per-step persistent storage and a device active-request count for empty ranks, rejected tokens and length bounds.
- Retains current main's forward-time NoPE metadata planning and updates its persistent valid-row mask.
- Preallocates secondary KV-group block tables for FULL buckets exceeding `max_num_seqs`.
- Replaces the GDN padding upload with device-side boundary clamping and adds profiler ranges for first-pass preparation and graph execution.

The smaller-step path is restricted to GLM multi-KV-group MTP on A5 NoPE, TP=1, PCP=DCP=1, uniform decode, FULL draft graphs and dynamic MC2 `global_bs`. Existing fallback paths remain for other topologies.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Supported GLM-5.3-Flash MTP graph decoding performs less padded later-step work and avoids the diagnosed GDN upload stall. No option is added. Restart/recapture is required for a changed graph.

This is a **Draft** until the extracted current-main branch completes NPU graph replay and model output/acceptance validation.

### How was this patch tested?

- Extracted onto upstream `34c9170739ccc7ae6b05282febd51de72e9a5e47`, retaining its newer NoPE planning implementation.
- CPU-only regression with repository mocks: **148 passed, 13 skipped** across the four focused suites below plus `tests/ut/spec_decode/test_eagle_proposer.py`. The index-sharing fixture now explicitly sets `CUDAGraphMode.NONE`, matching the forward-context contract:
  - `tests/ut/ops/test_gdn_padding_device_view.py`
  - `tests/ut/spec_decode/test_glm5next_mtp_graph_metadata.py`
  - `tests/ut/spec_decode/test_multi_kv_cache_group_proposer.py`
  - `tests/ut/attention/test_sfa_nope_metadata.py`
- Coverage includes changing active counts, empty ranks, rejection/length boundaries, stable graph storage and oversized secondary-group tables.
- Ruff check/format and `git diff --check` passed.
- `format.sh ci` could not run its hooks because pre-commit is not installed. CI is not claimed to have passed.

Earlier A5 evidence is from integration revision `8d5969cc00db06a8cbf3e654c2358ef440435c82`, **not a new measurement of this extracted PR**. With MTP=5, FP8 caches, 32 requests of 262156–262158 input tokens and fixed DP8 distribution [5,2,2,4,2,5,7,5], capture began after prefill/KV reception. Prompt counters did not increase, waiting was zero and there were no preemptions.

| Integration case | Steady iterations | Target first Dispatch arrival P50/P99 (ms) | Iteration period P50/P99 (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Graph before GDN padding fix, 5 s | 101 | 4.067 / 4.699 | 52.120 / 52.743 |
| Graph after GDN padding fix, 5 s | 108 | 0.639 / 1.141 | 48.472 / 49.150 |
| Fixed graph, 20 s | 411 | 0.671 / 1.794 | 48.697 / 49.725 |

The matched 5-second comparison isolates the GDN padding fix within the integration; it is not an isolated benchmark of every change in this PR. The 20-second run completed 32×4096 generated tokens. Standalone A5 GDN padding validation passed 5 cases, and the old upload fails the CPU negative control. Arrival spread/iteration period are profiler metrics, not token TPOT or formal no-profiler throughput.

Residual late graph submissions remain (worst arrival spread 3.098 ms in the 20-second capture). The original 416.8 ms extreme tail did not recur, which does not prove elimination under all workloads. Eager-worker shutdown malloc corruption/SIGABRT remains unresolved and is not claimed fixed here.

items.title: [Performance][GDN] Skip layout conversion for suppressed intermediates
items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

`chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd` needs `h` and `v_new` in their working layout for `chunk_fwd_o`, but the caller does not receive those intermediates when `SUPPRESS_LEVEL < 3`. Previously, the function converted both tensors to BF16, transposed them, and made them contiguous before checking that level, then returned `None` for both.

This PR changes only `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/fla/chunk.py`. The output `o` is still converted as before, and `h`/`v_new` are still computed and consumed by `chunk_fwd_o`. The two output-format conversions now run inside the `SUPPRESS_LEVEL >= 3` branch:

- Below level 3, the function returns the same `(g, o, A, final_state, None, None, None)` tuple without the two final return-layout conversions of `h` and `v_new`.
- At level 3 or above, it performs the same BF16, transpose, and contiguous operations as before and returns `(g, o, A, final_state, w, h, v_new)` in the same layout.

This removes two unnecessary conversion/copy chains from the suppressed-intermediate path. It does not skip the GDN computation or change the numerical operations that produce `o` or `final_state`.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No. The public API, return values, and configuration are unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

The local serving A/B used Qwen3.8-27B on two Ascend 910B3 NPUs (Atlas A2, TP=2), BF16, 100000 input tokens per request (80000 shared-prefix + 20000 unique), 16 output tokens, and concurrency 8. Both runs used the same local vLLM Ascend baseline (`0.19.1rc2.dev1283+g9bf964cb4`), including the existing BNSD patch and environment fixes; the intended code difference was this GDN conversion change. Both configurations completed the serving run successfully.

| Metric | Baseline | Optimized | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Queue time | 28.257 s | 27.678 s | -2.05% |
| TTFT | 46.538 s | 45.872 s | -1.43% |

vLLM main baseline: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

items.title: [Performance][Worker] Reuse GDN speculative decode metadata on Model Runner V1
items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Model Runner V1 rebuilds GDN attention metadata before every speculative decode replay. Even a batch containing only speculative decode requests repeats mixed-batch classification, sequence partitioning and token-index construction across compatible attention/cache groups. This adds CPU preparation work between model forwards.

Add a guarded pure speculative decode path using scheduler-owned CPU query boundaries and draft counts. Reuse read-only mask/token-index views and share only the request classification within one runner metadata-build call. Each group still refreshes its own physical state indices, current accepted-token counts and graph padding. Unsupported, mixed, prefill and empty batches retain the existing path. The per-call cache is never carried into the drafter or the next iteration.

### Dependencies and integration order

For the GLM-5.3-Flash CANN deployment used to develop and validate this optimization, apply **#18295 -> #16730 -> this PR**:

- #18295 supplies the Triton cache/metadata/index adapters used by the CANN pooled indexer.
- #16730 depends on #18295 and integrates CANN KeyPool/PoolKeyIndexer, including layer/draft metadata buffer reuse.
- This PR adds the complementary GDN CPU metadata optimization. It preserves their KPool/tail buffer ownership and MTP reuse rules.

Latest dependency heads reviewed: #16730 `0f205dbc004fd582956d796cf9d989e9ee0d0387`, #18295 `1c9916b008812b7e4b9039a89aeb1efab3f77302`. The three files touched here are identical between main `da519923fe88a0c90c499b6975727b58e78eb3cb` and the reviewed #16730 head; the patch applies cleanly to both.

These are **GLM deployment/integration-validation dependencies**, not additional imports required by the generic GDN fast path. This PR targets main and contains only its own three-file change; prerequisite commits are not duplicated in the diff. Joint GLM validation must include both dependency PRs. #18470 and #18473 are not prerequisites.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No new flags, environment variables or serving API changes. Compatible Model Runner V1 FULL speculative decode batches avoid redundant CPU metadata work. AscendC/Triton kernels and graph synchronization are unchanged. This reduces one source of forward gaps; it does not claim zero device idle time or a measured current-head full-model speedup.

### How was this patch tested?

**Current publication candidate:**
- Rebased onto main `da51992`; patch application checks passed against main and reviewed #16730.
- Repository-pinned Ruff 0.14.0 lint passed for all three files; formatting checks passed for the GDN builder and its test file.
- Python syntax compilation passed for all three files.
- Joint CPU tests on the current integration stack: candidate **131 passed, 2 failed**; baseline **109 passed, the same 2 failed**. All **22 new GDN regression cases passed**. Both failures are in the #18295 test fixture, which replaces Triton math helpers with MagicMock and raises TypeError; they are not counted as passing.
- Current-stack NPU pooled-cache adapter tests: **9 passed, 3 warnings**. These validate the dependency adapters, not the full-model performance benefit of this GDN optimization.
- Full `bash format.sh ci` and hardware/integration CI remain pending.

**Current full-model validation attempt (2026-10-13):**
- Common baseline: main `da51992` + #18295 `1c9916b` + #16730 `0f205db`; candidate differs only by this PR `dee4b26` (three files).
- GLM-5.3-Flash W8A8, single node DP8 / TP2 / EP16, MTP5, C90, 2048 input / 4096 output, seed 1024, temperature 0, ignore EOS, max length 133120, prefix cache disabled, FULL_DECODE_ONLY target and non-eager drafter. Planned measurement: three unprofiled rounds per arm, followed by a separate 8-step CPU/NPU profile.
- After resources became available, the baseline loaded and enabled graph replay, but failed during C90 prewarm (128 output tokens, excluded from measurement). The first device error was `GatherV3<float, int64>` rejecting indices **-4 through -1** for range `[0, 136665)`; HCCL watchdog failures followed.
- This baseline contains no GDN optimization from this PR. The candidate was not started, and no timed 2048/4096 round or profile completed. **No current-head TPOT, throughput or device-idle improvement is claimed.** The baseline runtime failure must be resolved before a matched comparison can be completed.

**Historical validation of this optimization, before this rebase:**
- 93 GDN UT and 151 related runner/MTP/KDA UT passed.
- Six NPU metadata comparisons at 12 -> 10 -> 1 -> 11 -> 16 -> 2 live requests, padded to 16, matched the original path field by field and retained graph input addresses.
- CPU-only microbenchmark with 8 synthetic groups: about 3.40 -> 0.92 ms per metadata build, approximately 73% lower preparation time. This is not the real model's group count or a full-model TPOT/idle improvement.
- Those results used #16730 `45daa4de7b9c495795853feefa69f7d1aa17bc8b` plus #18295 `e3b9e286a517626c8182ba10bc6ee536998c593a`; the six NPU metadata comparisons and CPU microbenchmark have not been rerun for the latest dependency stack.

Keep this PR draft until current-head joint correctness, dynamic/padded MTP replay and matched full-model performance validation complete.

### What this PR does / why we need it?
This PR integrates two ops-transformer GDN operators into the Ascend 310P  linear-attention path:

  - `gdn_ops_ext.fused_gdn_gating`
  - `gdn_ops_ext.chunk_gated_delta_rule_compute_wy`

The implementation lazily loads the external `gdn_ops_ext` PyTorch extension  and dispatches supported inputs through:

  - `torch.ops.gdn_ops_ext.fused_gdn_gating`
  - `torch.ops.gdn_ops_ext.chunk_gated_delta_rule_compute_wy`

The existing PyTorch implementations are retained as fallbacks when the  extension is unavailable or the input shape, dtype, device, or chunk size is  unsupported.

The two operators are packaged in one ops-transformer extension with a  dedicated `gdn_ops_ext` namespace. This avoids the package and operator  registration conflicts caused by installing multiple independent  `custom_ops` extensions.

No C++ custom-op registration is added to vllm-ascend. The underlying ACLNN  operators and the PyTorch extension are provided by ops-transformer.

This change improves the performance of the Qwen3.5 GDN/linear-attention path  on Ascend 310P while preserving the existing fallback behavior.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
On Ascend 310P, models using the GDN linear-attention path can use the  optimized ops-transformer implementations when `gdn_ops_ext` and the required  ACLNN operator packages are installed.

There is no change to the public vLLM API or model output contract. If the  extension is unavailable or an input is unsupported, execution automatically  falls back to the existing PyTorch implementation.

 Ran `tests/ut/_310p/ops/test_gdn_ops_ext_dispatch_310.py`.

 All 6 tests passed. The tests cover loading `gdn_ops_ext`, dispatching both   GDN operators, forwarding operator arguments, and falling back to the   PyTorch implementations for unavailable or unsupported inputs.

  3. **Qwen3.5-2B serving performance test**

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR consolidates Ascend 310P Gated DeltaNet (GDN) prefill improvements and fixes correctness issues in the optimized execution path.

items.title: [Performance][GDN] Share group-invariant metadata across kv-cache groups

labels.name: ready-precise
labels.description: run selected e2e test for pr

items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

**Background**

Hybrid models such as Qwen3.8 / Qwen4-Exp (e.g. Qwen3.8-27B) interleave
GDN (linear-attention) layers and full-attention layers at 3:1. The hybrid KV cache
manager aligns kv-cache group sizes to the least-numerous layer type, which splits
the GDN layers across **3 kv-cache groups**. As a result, `_build_attn_group_metadata`
invokes the GDN metadata builder's `build()` once per group on **every step**.

Within a single `_build_attention_metadata` call, every GDN group receives an
identical `common_attn_metadata` **except its own `block_table_tensor` /
`slot_mapping`**. However, the full metadata pipeline is executed 3x per step:

- spec sequence classification + fold (1 `.item()` host sync per group)
- batch statistics (4 `.item()` host syncs per group)
- stable argsort + `repeat_interleave` token reorder
- spec / non-spec `query_start_loc` cumsums and accepted-token reorder
- chunked-prefill chunk indices/offsets (6 CPU `prepare_*` calls + H2D per group)
- causal conv1d metadata and `has_initial_state`

**What this PR changes**

- Add `GDNGroupInvariantCache` to `gdn_attn_builder.py`.
- `AscendGDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build()` accepts an optional
  `group_invariant_cache` argument.
- The model runner creates one cache before the kv-cache-group loop and passes it
  to every GDN group's build. The **first group (fingerprint miss) performs the
  full build and fills the cache**; subsequent groups **reuse the group-invariant
  intermediates and only recompute the state-index tensors derived from their own
  block table**.

Effect per step: host-device syncs drop from 3x5 to 5; the argsort,
chunked-prefill metadata and conv1d metadata drop from 3x to 1x.

**Safety properties**

- Only block-table-independent results are cached. `spec_state_indices_tensor`,
  `non_spec_state_indices_tensor` and `prefill_state_indices` are always
  recomputed from each group's own block table.
- Cached tensors are shared read-only; per-group full-graph padding still writes
  each builder's own persistent buffers, so captured graph addresses are unchanged.
- An O(1) shape-level fingerprint falls back to a full build on any mismatch.
- Callers that pass no cache (drafting, cudagraph capture, external callers)
  keep the original path unchanged.
- Guarded to non-ubatched calls (`ubid is None`): the shape-level fingerprint
  cannot distinguish same-shaped ubatches, so ubatched GDN builds fall back to
  full computation instead of silently reusing stale entries.

This mirrors the existing DSA precedent (`shared_dsa_draft_cache`).

### Benchmark

**GDN metadata `build()` per-step cost** (single forward):
- **Before**: all 3 kv-cache groups each run the full build, ~`2.1 ms/group`, total `6.3 ms`.
- **After**: the first group still builds fully (`2.1 ms`); the 2nd and 3rd groups
  reuse the cache (`1.2 ms` each), total `4.5 ms`.
- Saves **~1.8 ms / step (≈28.6%)** per forward. With speculative decoding
  (MTP, k=3) this is another forward per step, so the wall-clock benefit compounds.

**End-to-end benchmark** — Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, TP=2, 8k-token random input, 350 output tokens:

| Metric                | Before   | After    | Δ        |
|-----------------------|----------|----------|----------|
| Throughput (tokens/s) | 222.28   | 227.36   | +2.29%   |
| TTFT (ms)             | 1162.65  | 1156.24  | -0.55%   |
| TPOT (ms)             | 23.21    | 22.74    | -2.03%   |
| E2E Latency (ms)      | 9262.48  | 9094.04  | -1.82%   |

Throughput improves by **+2.29%**, and TTFT / TPOT / E2E latency all drop
(by roughly 0.6% ~ 2%). The win comes entirely from removing the redundant
host-device syncs (`.item()`), the repeated NPU argsort, and the duplicated
chunked-prefill / conv1d metadata across the 3 GDN groups.

**Accuracy regression check** — GPQA-diamond benchmark:

| Dataset       | Before | After |
|--------------|--------|-------|
| GPQA-diamond | 0.8622 | 0.868 |

Accuracy is preserved (0.8622 → 0.868), confirming the metadata reuse does not
degrade output quality.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This is a pure internal optimization of attention metadata construction.
No API, configuration or behavior change. The produced metadata is field-by-field
identical to the original full build (verified by UTs).

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds a built-in AscendC operator to optimize the QKV layout transformation in the Gated DeltaNet (GDN).

The GDN projection produces a token-major packed tensor:

```text
[Q0 K0 V0] [Q1 K1 V1] ...
```

The downstream recurrent and chunk GDN kernels consume three contiguous Q, K, and V tensors:

```text
[Q0 Q1 ...] [K0 K1 ...] [V0 V1 ...]
```

The existing PyTorch implementation splits the packed tensor, flattens the three non-contiguous views, and concatenates them. Profiling shows that this path launches three copy kernels followed by one concatenation kernel. The host-side dispatch chain delays submission of the following operators, while Q/K/V data is also copied through intermediate buffers.

This PR replaces that sequence with one AIC-only AscendC kernel. The kernel partitions token rows across cores and uses DMA `DataCopy` operations to move Q, K, and V directly to their final contiguous regions. The Python wrapper then creates the existing output views without additional NPU kernels.

The change includes:

- the `RearrangeQkvDma` AscendC kernel, host definition, and tiling implementation;
- registration in the vLLM Ascend built-in custom-operator build for A2 and A3;
- PrivateUse1 and Meta implementations for `torch.ops._C_ascend.npu_rearrange_qkv`;
- dispatch from the existing GDN path when the input is contiguous BF16 or FP16 and the Q/K/V widths satisfy the 32-byte DMA alignment requirement;
- fallback to the existing vLLM implementation on unsupported devices or layouts.

The mathematical operation, output shapes, and GDN state update order are unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. There is no new API or configuration option. Supported GDN workloads select the optimized implementation automatically, while unsupported workloads keep the existing behavior.

Qwen3.5-9B retains its original 38 cache groups; a compatible 24-GDN-group batch performs one common build plus 23 physical-state updates.

- Reuse bounded decode-layout templates and group-local captured state views. Refresh current accepted counts, query boundaries, recurrent lengths, physical states and padding every step. Unsupported layouts, checkpoints and custom providers retain independent builds.
- Gather aligned Mamba indices and batch graph-state copies into existing captured storage, retaining pointer owners and handling strided sources and padded rows. Cache row views by pointer/shape/stride/dtype/device, never their values.

items.title: [Performance] Fix KV cache group fracturing caused by single-layer PLE cache
items.body:
> **Base PR.** Follow-up to #15162 (which in turn builds on #15072). The base PR must land first;
> this PR only adds the KV cache group coalescing described below and keeps the same target branch
> (`releases/v0.26.0rc`). Without #15162 / #15072 the hybrid QSA/PLE/six-slab cache layout that this
> PR re-groups does not exist.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

**Problem.** Hybrid KV cache grouping buckets layers by *exact* `KVCacheSpec` equality and then uses
the **smallest bucket** as the group size. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next has 36 identical GDN layers but also a
**single PLE state cache layer** (one state shape) next to its QSA raw/compressed caches, so the
smallest bucket is 1. The group size collapses to 1 and the 36 GDN layers are split into **36
one-layer groups** — **39 groups** after the QSA composite merge contributed by #15162.

**Why it matters.** Each KV cache group owns its own attention metadata builder, and
`_build_attention_metadata` builds metadata once per (group, attention group). GDN metadata is
therefore rebuilt **36 times per decode step instead of 3**, repeating identical host-side work
(sequence split, argsort, chunked-prefill index prep) every time, with 33 redundant builders each
holding a pinned buffer of `max_num_seqs * (num_spec + 1)` entries. A plain 3:1 hybrid without a rare
single-layer cache (e.g. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, smallest bucket 12) has 3 GDN groups and no such problem.

**What this PR does.** Adds `_merge_shattered_gdn_groups()` to the Ascend `get_kv_cache_groups()`
hook, running after upstream grouping and before the QSA composite merge. It re-buckets by spec
equality exactly like upstream, recomputes the group size over **multi-layer buckets only** so a
genuinely single-layer rare type no longer drags the granularity down, and merges a bucket **only
when all of its layers are currently singleton groups with identical specs**, reusing upstream's
strided layer assignment and spec merge (which keeps upstream's "all layers in one group must have
the same spec" assertion intact).

**Result.** `kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups` **39 → 6** (3 GDN + PLE + QSA composite + QSA raw),
GDN `build()` **36 → 3** per decode step. The change is confined to
`vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_kv_cache_utils.py` (+105 lines); no other file is touched and no
existing logic is modified.

**Scope and safety.**

- Models without a multi-layer GDN bucket return immediately; already-healthy groupings (e.g.
  Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) hit the "not shattered" guard and are a no-op.
- The six-region memory planner from #15162 keys physical tensors by layer *role*, and group ids are
  only consulted to decide whether QSA main and compressed share a block table — so the six-slab
  physical layout and every tensor shape/offset are unchanged, and the logical cache groups stay
  valid.
- The memory-usage estimate keeps the upstream per-group summation shape; for `MambaSpec` the
  per-group term is independent of how many layers the group holds, so 3 groups is the accurate
  reservation whereas 36 groups was a 12x over-estimate.
- Downstream consumers are group-count agnostic: the coordinator already co-locates groups with equal
  specs, `get_mamba_groups()` aggregates by distinct spec, scheduling-parameter validation checks
  spec fields rather than layer counts, and block-size resolution uses `lcm`/`gcd`, which are
  invariant once duplicate block sizes are removed.

As a side effect the change also drops 33 per-group block tables, 33 KV cache managers and 33 mamba
state-copy group iterations per step.

Follow-up to #15162.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. There is no API, CLI, config or environment-variable change, and model output is unchanged. The
only observable difference is one INFO log line (re-grouped layer count, new group count, group size)
emitted when the re-grouping actually triggers. Models without a rare single-layer Mamba cache are
completely unaffected.

### How was this patch tested?

Environment: Ascend A2, w8a8 quantized weights, MTP enabled, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, on top of #15162.

1. Group count printed after attention-backend initialization: **39 before → 6 after**.
2. `gdn_attn_builder::build` occurrences within a single decode step in a MindStudio Insight profile:
   **36 before → 3 after**.
3. Regression: identical print on a 3:1 hybrid without a rare single-layer cache (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B)
   reports the same grouping before and after the patch (4 groups, GDN = 3), confirming the new path
   is a no-op there.
4. Unit tests: `pytest -sv tests/ut/core/test_six_region_kv_cache_layout.py`.

No new unit test is added: the grouping outcome depends on a full `get_kv_cache_spec()` pass over a
hybrid model, so it is verified end-to-end with the counters above. A focused unit test asserting the
39 → 6 split can be added if reviewers prefer.

items.title: [Performance] Fuse rearrange_mixed_qkv and fused_gdn_gating on Ascend A2/A3
items.body:
### What does this PR do, and why?

The Qwen GDN path rearranges token-major mixed QKV into contiguous Q, K, and V buffers, then computes GDN gating separately. On Ascend A2/A3 this produces multiple copy/concat launches followed by a gating launch, even though the two pieces of work are independent.

This PR adds **one** custom operator, `npu_fused_rearrange_mix_qkv_gdn_gating`. Its `MIX_AIC_1_2` kernel runs QKV DMA on AIC and GDN gating on AIV in the same launch. It returns packed QKV, FP32 `g`, and BF16 `beta`. The operator supports the model's actual mixed head parameter types (`A_log` FP32 and `dt_bias` BF16) as well as matching FP32/BF16/FP16 head parameter types. Gating nonlinearities compute in FP32, as in the existing Triton implementation; this conversion occurs inside the kernel, without an additional device launch or intermediate GM tensor.

`A2A3DeviceAdaptor` dispatches to the fused operator. Other device families retain the existing split path. A batch containing both speculative and non-speculative QKV inputs also retains the split path because neither input contains all of the gating rows. The operator has PrivateUse1 and Meta registrations, handles zero tokens, and validates its direct-call input contract at the C++ boundary. This PR does **not** add or depend on a standalone `rearrange_qkv_dma` operator.

### User-facing change

No public API or configuration change. Eligible A2/A3 GDN calls use the fused operator automatically; other device families and mixed speculative batches retain their existing behavior.

### Timeline evidence

The following captures show the relevant GDN region of a Qwen3.6-27B graph run. Before the change, QKV rearrangement appears as copy/concat work followed by `fused_gdn_gating_kernel`. After the change, that region contains `FusedRearrangeMixQkvGdnGating` instead. The screenshots' selected spans (34.5 µs before and 10.4 µs after) are illustrative timeline selections, **not** the operator-level benchmark result.

Before:

![Before: copy and concat followed by fused GDN gating](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7c6800a5-5c6e-4b96-92f4-e1b22db1a9fb)

After:

![After: fused rearrangement and gating operator](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aa1a35ea-c555-477e-8071-d1259a77da4a)

### End-to-end serving performance

Qwen3.6-27B, TP=2, FULL_AND_DECODE enabled; prompt length 1024, generation length 512, maximum request concurrency 8, 128 requests. The table compares the reported median benchmark runs. Both variants completed all 128 requests with zero failures; each generated 65,536 output tokens from 132,393 input tokens.

| Metric | Before | After | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 191.07 | 197.10 | +3.16% |
| Total token throughput (tok/s) | 577.05 | 595.28 | +3.16% |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 38.34 | 37.06 | −3.34% |
| Median end-to-end latency (ms) | 21,434.25 | 20,779.10 | −3.06% |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 1,842.71 | 1,837.10 | −0.30% |
| Benchmark duration (s) | 343.00 | 332.50 | −3.06% |

The improvement is concentrated in generation latency; TTFT is nearly unchanged. These are serving-level results, not an operator-only speedup.
