items.title: [Performance][KV Cache] Re-group shattered GDN layers to cut Qwen3.8 KV cache groups from 39 to 6
items.body:
> 🔗 Stacked on #16981 (`feat/qwen38-flash-next-main-v1`). Please review after #16981; it must not be merged before it.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

**Problem.** For hybrid models upstream `_get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size` derives `group_size` from the *smallest* spec bucket. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next carries a single rare PLE cache layer (`ple_layer_ids: [2]`) whose `MambaSpec` declares a conv state only (`len(shapes) == 1`), next to 36 identical GDN layers. That minimum is therefore 1, so the GDN bucket — which a hybrid without the rare type (e.g. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) groups into 3 groups of 12 — is shattered into 36 one-layer KV cache groups:

```
bucket sizes: { GDN: 36, PLE: 1, QSA main: 12, QSA compressed: 12, QSA raw: 12 }
group_size   = min(...) = 1
GDN          = cdiv(36, 1) = 36 singleton groups
```

Every KV cache group gets its own attention metadata builder and its own row in the block table / slot mapping, so `_build_attention_metadata` rebuilds GDN metadata **36 times per step instead of 3**, and each extra builder also pins its own `max_num_seqs × (num_spec + 1)` buffers.

**Fix.** After upstream grouping (and before the QSA composite merge) re-group the GDN layers that upstream shattered, using the same sizing rule and the same strided layer assignment upstream uses, but computing `group_size` over the **multi-layer** buckets only, so a genuine singleton type (PLE) can no longer drag the GDN granularity down:

```python
multi_sizes = [len(layers) for layers in same_type_layers.values() if len(layers) > 1]
group_size = min(multi_sizes)
```

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `len(kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups)` | 39 | **6** |
| `AscendGDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build()` per step | 36 | **3** |
| `_build_attn_group_metadata` calls per step | 40 | **7** |
| GDN block tables / slot-mapping rows / builder instances | 36 | **3** |

**Scope of the change.** One function plus one call site in `vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_kv_cache_utils.py` (`_merge_shattered_gdn_groups`, called from `_get_ascend_kv_cache_groups`). It is a no-op unless a GDN bucket is *fully* shattered:

- buckets whose specs are not bit-identical are never merged (`KVCacheSpec.merge` asserts equality, so heterogeneous specs can never land in one group);
- buckets that are already multi-layer, or only *partially* shattered, are left untouched;
- GLM5-Next returns earlier, non-Mamba models never reach the rewrite;
- `is_eagle_group` is propagated to the regrouped blocks.

**Memory layout is unchanged.** The six-region planner keys physical tensors by layer *role* (GDN / PLE / QSA_MAIN / QSA_RAW / QSA_COMPRESSED), assigns each owner a `slot` by its index *within the role*, and only consults `owner_group_ids` to decide whether QSA main and compressed share a block table (`vllm_ascend/core/six_region_kv_cache_layout.py:252`). Rows come from `_owner_sort_key`, not from group membership, so offsets, slots, `slot_count` and `slot_backing_size` are identical before and after.

Refs #16981

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Grouping is an internal derivation from the KV cache specs; no API, config or numerical behavior changes. The only observable difference is one informational log line, and a smaller group count:

```
Ascend re-grouped 36 shattered GDN layers into 3 KV cache groups (group_size=12);
GDN attention metadata will be built 3 times per step instead of 36.
Using QSA six-region grouping: ... 6 total cache groups
```

items.title: [Performance][Ops] Split fused qkvz projection into separate qkv and z linears in GDN

labels.name: ready-precise
labels.description: run selected e2e test for pr

items.body: ### What this PR does / why we need it? In `vllm_ascend/ops/gdn.py`, `AscendGatedDeltaNetAttention.forward` previously computed the fused `qkvz` input projection and then split the output tensor into `mixed_qkv` and `z`. For the non-interleaved GQA layout used by Qwen3.5 (`gqa_interleaved_layout=False`), this PR adds a fast path that splits the projection weight up front and computes the two parts with independent `torch.nn.functional.linear` calls: ```python qkv_size = (self.key_dim * 2 + self.value_dim) // self.tp_size z_size = self.value_dim // self.tp_size use_weight_split = ( getattr(self, "quant_config", None) is None and isinstance( getattr(self.in_proj_qkvz, "quant_method", None), UnquantizedLinearMethod, ) ) if use_weight_split: qkvz_weight = self.in_proj_qkvz.weight mixed_qkv = torch.nn.functional.linear( hidden_states, qkvz_weight[:qkv_size] ) z = torch.nn.functional.linear( hidden_states, qkvz_weight[qkv_size:] ) else: mixed_qkvz, _ = self.in_proj_qkvz(hidden_states) mixed_qkv, z = mixed_qkvz.split([qkv_size, z_size], dim=-1) ``` The weight-split path is restricted to genuinely unquantized models. Quantized models continue to use the projection module's normal `forward` path before splitting the result. This guard is required for the quantized Qwen3.5 regression identified during review. ModelSlim checkpoints can leave Qwen3.5 GDN projections marked as `FLOAT` while quantizing surrounding MoE layers as `W8A8_DYNAMIC`. Even in that case, `AscendUnquantizedLinearMethod` may pack the stored weight in `FRACTAL_NZ` format. Applying `F.linear` directly to the stored weight would bypass the required Ascend weight handling and produce incorrect results. Why the unquantized fast path is useful: - Avoids materializing the full `mixed_qkvz` intermediate tensor. - Avoids the explicit `tensor.split` on the projected output. - Produces `z` as a fresh contiguous tensor, allowing the following reshape to remain a view. - Avoids tuple/bias handling in `MergedColumnParallelLinear.forward` when it is safe to do so. - Preserves the quantization method and custom-op path for quantized configurations. The interleaved-layout Qwen3-Next branch and the separate `in_proj_qkv` / `in_proj_z` branch are unchanged. ### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change? No. This is an internal projection refactor. For unquantized models, the new path is numerically equivalent to the previous fused-projection-then-split implementation. For quantized models, the original quantization-aware projection path is preserved to avoid accuracy regressions. ### How was this patch tested? - Added `tests/ut/ops/test_gdn_qkvz_split.py`. - Verified numerical equivalence across four shape and tensor-parallel configurations, including `tp_size=2`. - Added a regression test confirming that the unquantized fast path bypasses `in_proj_qkvz.forward`. - Added packed INT8 coverage confirming that quantized weights use the module `forward` path. - Added coverage for the Qwen3.5 mixed configuration where GDN projections are `FLOAT` but the model has an active quantization configuration. ```text pytest -q tests/ut/ops/test_gdn_qkvz_split.py 7 passed ``` Focused GDN unit tests also pass: ```text pytest -q \ tests/ut/ops/test_gdn_qkvz_split.py \ tests/ut/ops/test_gdn_attn_builder.py \ tests/ut/ops/test_gdn_chunk_meta.py 35 passed ``` - E2E greedy-generation coverage: `tests/e2e/pull_request/four_card/test_qwen3_5.py` for Qwen3.5-27B dense and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B MoE models. - TP2 hardware smoke test completed successfully with `Eco-Tech/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8` on NPU 8 and NPU 9. - GPQA test result on `Eco-Tech/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8`: - `py_compile` and `git diff --check` pass. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ba07e4a48fc951300d97eb506217dd530583dea3 - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

items.title: [Performance] Fuse the Qwen3.5 GDN decode pipeline on Ascend
items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Qwen3.5-9B GDN decode currently materializes full intermediate tensors and launches separate operators for causal convolution, Q/K normalization, gating, the recurrent update, and gated RMSNorm. For single-token decode, these operators repeatedly read and write the same head-local data, so launch and memory-traffic overhead dominate their small amount of arithmetic.

This PR adds an opt-in Triton kernel that preserves the same GDN equations but decomposes the work by GQA group. Each program processes one Q/K head together with its two V/Z heads and directly continues through convolution state update, Q/K L2 normalization, gate construction, recurrent-state update, and gated RMSNorm. This avoids the full-tensor materialization barriers between those steps.

The patch is based on the current `releases/v0.23.0` branch at `d68bb5e`. Its diff is limited to the GDN implementation, Qwen3.5 GDN dispatch, the GDN environment switch, and focused GDN tests. It does not include the separate RMSNorm--MatMul experiment, its AscendC sources, bindings, build changes, or Qwen3.5 MLP patch.

The integration also keeps runtime decode selection behind vLLM's existing `qwen_gdn_attention_core` custom-op boundary. This is required for graph mode: the initial compile/profile pass does not carry attention metadata, and tracing the Python branch directly would otherwise permanently capture the original path.

The optimized path is deliberately narrow and falls back to the existing implementation unless all of the following hold:

- `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_GDN_DECODE_TILE_PIPELINE=1`;
- Qwen3.5-9B GDN layout, BF16, and convolution width 4;
- TP=1 or TP=2;
- non-speculative decode with no prefill tokens;
- real decode batch size from 1 through 16.

Prefill, speculative decoding, unsupported dtypes/shapes, and other models keep the original path.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, it adds the optional environment variable `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_GDN_DECODE_TILE_PIPELINE`. It defaults to `0`, so existing behavior is unchanged unless users explicitly enable the optimization.

### How was this patch tested?

#### Unit tests

```bash
pytest -q tests/ut/ops/test_gdn_attn_builder.py
```

Result: `22 passed`. New cases cover graph-safe custom-op dispatch, PIECEWISE projection/metadata padding, and fallback for unsupported dtype and TP modes.

#### Testbed

- Ascend 910B3, BF16, Qwen3.5-9B, vLLM 0.23.0;
- exclusive NPU allocation for each A/B implementation;
- original and optimized paths compared with identical model and workload configuration.

The exhaustive results below were collected on the pre-cleanup experimental branch. The GDN patch carried into this PR is semantically identical: cleanup only replaced repeated literals with named constants and applied formatting, the base-branch update did not modify any of the five GDN PR paths, and the separate RMSNorm--MatMul switch remained disabled throughout the measurements. A reduced confirmation on the exact PR head is reported separately below.

#### Exact PR-head reduced confirmation

The clean PR commit `59b249e6` was deployed independently and its five changed file hashes were checked against the local worktree before the run. The reduced matrix used B=1/16, prefill=16/1024, decode=256, TP=1/2, and eager, PIECEWISE, and FULL+FX execution. Original and optimized processes were interleaved in ABBA/BAAB order. TP1 used two independent device replicas; every shape had at least 12 samples per implementation for TP1 and six for TP2.

|   TP | Mode      | Cases | Geomean wall-time speedup |         Range | Faster cases | Mean TPOT reduction |
| ---: | --------- | ----: | ------------------------: | ------------: | -----------: | ------------------: |
|    1 | eager     |     4 |                    1.496x | 1.477--1.533x |          4/4 |              33.73% |
|    1 | PIECEWISE |     4 |                    1.687x | 1.599--1.729x |          4/4 |              42.40% |

|    2 | PIECEWISE |     4 |                    1.784x | 1.717--1.841x |          4/4 |              44.91% |
|    2 | FULL + FX |     4 |                    1.095x | 0.806--1.455x |          3/4 |               8.59% |

All 36 independent benchmark processes and 144 measured shape records completed without failure. The small FULL+FX matrix showed high TP2 variance, including a slower B=16/prefill=16 shape, while its geomean and mean TPOT remained improved; the larger original campaign below observed 29/30 faster TP2 FULL+FX cases.

Probability precision was then checked on the same exact commit with FULL+FX, decode=64, B=1/16, prefill=16/1024, TP=1/2, and captured top-20 log-probabilities. Each TP used an Original/Fused/Original-repeat sequence. Only positions whose preceding token context remained identical in all compared runs were included; 7,403 such comparison positions were processed overall.

|   TP | Comparison                  | Paired positions | Argmax agreement | Mean top-1 probability error | P99 top-1 probability error |
| ---: | --------------------------- | ---------------: | ---------------: | ---------------------------: | --------------------------: |
|    1 | Original vs Fused           |            1,654 |          99.516% |                     0.002016 |                    0.030316 |
|    1 | Original vs Original repeat |            1,654 |          99.758% |                     0.001579 |                    0.029818 |

For TP1, the A/B mean top-1 error above the independent-run A/A baseline was 0.000437; for TP2 it was 0.001900. These bounded differences are expected from the changed BF16 operation order and are not evidence of a different real-number algorithm. The test does not claim full-vocabulary KL because only top-20 probabilities were captured.

#### Original validation campaign: operator path and numerical checks

- GDN decode path event latency improved by 5.86--6.26x for TP1/TP2 and B=1/2/4/8/16.
- Kernel-profiler attribution measured 14.13 us per optimized GDN layer versus 78.30 us for the selected original subchain, approximately 5.54x.
- Batched and per-request optimized executions were bit-identical, excluding cross-request state mixing.
- Maximum operator output difference was 0.11914062 and maximum recurrent-state difference was 0.02343604. These differences come from BF16 operation-order changes; the real-number equations are unchanged.

#### Original validation campaign: eager end-to-end Cartesian sweep

The sweep covered the Cartesian product of:

- batch: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16;
- prefill tokens: 16, 64, 256, 1024;
- decode tokens: 64, 256, 1024, 4096;
- TP: 1 and 2.

|    1 |    80 |                     1.59x |        79/80 |              38.68% |
|    2 |    80 |                     1.63x |        80/80 |              37.87% |

Each row contains 30 shape cases and at least six samples per implementation. There were no failed case records.

|   TP | Graph mode | Geomean speedup | Faster cases | Mean TPOT reduction |
| ---: | ---------- | --------------: | -----------: | ------------------: |
|    1 | PIECEWISE  |          1.682x |        30/30 |              43.62% |

FULL graph mode has a smaller gain because graph replay already removes much of the launch overhead; PIECEWISE mode retains the larger memory-traffic and synchronization benefit.

#### Original validation campaign: compatibility and quality

- Prefix caching: 12 cases per implementation completed.
- MTP: 4 cases per implementation completed and correctly used the original fallback path.
- Long case: B=16, prefill=1024, decode=4096 completed for both paths.
- Probability comparison across tested execution modes retained 99.57--99.67% top-1 agreement; the additional mean top-1 probability error was approximately 0.0011--0.0020.
- GSM8K 5-shot, 1,319 examples: strict exact match changed from 87.491% to 87.263% (-0.227 percentage points), below the reported single-run standard error of approximately 0.91 percentage points.
- WikiText-2 perplexity was identical: word perplexity 9.608194782 and byte perplexity 1.526718360 for both paths.

# [Performance][Operator] Emit w/u in head-first layout to skip redundant transposes in GDN chunk prefill

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR optimizes `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd` (GDN chunked prefill) on Ascend by eliminating redundant data transposes.

- **Emit `w`/`u` in head-first layout directly.** `recompute_w_u_fwd` gains a `HEAD_FIRST_OUTPUT` switch so `w`/`u` are produced as `[B, H, T, D]` instead of `[B, T, H, D]`. The two `.transpose(1, 2).contiguous()` calls in `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd` are then skipped — they were only needed to feed the AscendC kernel, which consumes head-first layout.

- **Make `v_new`/`h` writeback conditional.** The `v_new`/`h` transpose-and-contiguous writeback is moved into the `SUPPRESS_LEVEL >= 3` branch, since the main path (`SUPPRESS_LEVEL < 3`) only needs `o` and `final_state`.

- **Keep PCP and high-suppression compatibility.** `head_first_output = (not is_pcp) and (SUPPRESS_LEVEL < 3)`:
  - Under PCP (`world_size > 1`), `w`/`u` stay seq-major because `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_hupdate` requires seq-major addressing (`stride_w = H * K`);
  - Under `SUPPRESS_LEVEL >= 3`, the full return set (`w, h, v_new`) remains seq-major to preserve the API contract.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. The public `chunk_gated_delta_rule` API and output layouts (`o`, `final_state`) are unchanged; the `w`/`h`/`v_new` return contract is preserved under `SUPPRESS_LEVEL >= 3`.

### How was this patch tested?

- Existing unit tests in `tests/ut/ops/test_gdn_chunk_meta.py` pass (prebuilt metadata threading and PCP chaining are unaffected by the layout change).

- Consistency and performance were validated on Ascend with `compare_gdn_versions.py`, which runs identical inputs through the baseline and optimized kernels and compares `o`/`final_state` (max abs/rel diff) and median latency (speedup), covering varlen/non-varlen and T2048/T8192 cases.

- The head-first path was re-verified with the corrected `offs_t_2d` broadcasting under `SUPPRESS_LEVEL < 3` (the default).

items.title: [Feature] Add FLA RecurrentGDN Backend
items.body:
### Overview
This change introduces a switchable backend for the GDN decode recurrent operator. A new configuration item, `ascend_gdn_decode_backend`, allows selection between `fla_npu` and native custom operators. The mechanism covers all three decode paths:

| Path | Location |
| :--- | :--- |
| 2.1 MTP spec decode | `AscendGatedDeltaNetAttention.forward` spec branch |
| 2.2 Mixed-batch non-spec decode | `split_non_spec` decode branch |
| 2.3 Prefill chunk / pure decode | non-spec branch |

### Performance
We conducted tests across 50 scenarios at the single-operator level, comparing the performance of operators in the fla package against the original recurrent operators. For recurrent_gated_delta_rule, the fla implementation reduced the average latency from 538us to 148us.

### How to use
Add extra addtional-config : `vllm serve xxx --additional-config '"ascend_gdn_decode_backend": "fla_npu"`

items.title: [BugFix][310P] Preserve recurrent GDN state rows for ragged MTP
items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #17856 for the standalone Ascend 310P recurrent GDN operator.

With ragged MTP verification, the previous accepted-token count can exceed the current query length. The existing kernel rejects this legal case and returns before completing state/output updates. Removing that guard alone is insufficient: flattening the state table by current query lengths discards historical slots and can select another request's state.

This change preserves the full `[B, W]` state-index table. Host tiling passes its row stride to the kernel, which reads history at `row_start + accepted_prev - 1` and writes current states at `row_start + current_token_offset`. Acceptance bounds use the historical row width, independently of packed query offsets. The existing one-dimensional packed-index path remains supported. Zero-length padded requests are skipped before state access.

The new regression compares valid outputs and the entire state pool with a FP32 CPU recurrence. It exercises historical widths 2/3/4, accepted counts exceeding current lengths, shuffled physical state slots, heterogeneous batches, zero-length padding at different positions, trailing query-buffer padding, and the legacy one-dimensional path. Graph replay changes device-side lengths, accepted counts and state indices, and poisons the output buffer to expose unwritten values.

Related #18612 addresses the FLA path and does not modify this 310P kernel; this PR is confined to the 310P wrapper/host/kernel and its regression test.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Correct state selection and updates for legal ragged 310P MTP batches. The existing ssm_state_indices argument now accepts a two-dimensional per-request table as well as legacy one-dimensional packed indices. No new CLI options or Torch/ACLNN arguments. The internal tiling structure changes, so the host and device operator must be rebuilt together; mixed old/new binaries are unsupported.

### How was this patch tested?

- Atlas 300I DUO / Ascend 310P3, CANN 9.1, isolated custom OPP build:
  ```bash
  cd csrc
  bash build.sh --pkg --soc=ascend310p --ops=recurrent_gated_delta_rule_v310 -j4
  ```
- The exact pytest file in this PR was executed against the rebuilt OPP and patched wrapper on a real 310P3:
  ```bash
  python3 -m pytest -v tests/e2e/nightly/310p/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_recurrent_gdn_state_rows.py
  ```
  Result: **3 passed** (42 output/state assertions per mode, 126 total replayed cases). Maximum absolute error versus FP32 reference: output `7.63e-6`, FP16 state `1.22e-4`.
- Official image `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.23.0.post1-310p`, `Eco-Tech/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8` (including its own FLOAT MTP weights), with only this GDN OPP/wrapper overlaid: **TP2 + W8A8 + C16 KV + MTP2 + eager**, 8K context, max_num_seqs=4, no prefix caching. Four-client variable-prompt ordinary-text and strict JSON Schema smoke tests passed **16/16** (8 each). No W4/C8 or other experimental model patches loaded. This is official-image integration evidence, not a full current-main deployment or forced proof that every request exercised the ragged boundary.
- W8A8 TP1 failed during weight NZ format conversion due to NPU OOM before GDN execution. TP2 weights loaded (~20.59 GB/device), but Decode Graph startup in this older image failed in attention graph parameter update (`graph_params=None`). The successful W8A8 model test is explicitly **eager**; graph correctness is covered separately by the operator/wrapper regression.
- Supplementary real Qwen3.6-35B-A3B experimental W4A8 + MTP2 model: loading and Decode Graph capture passed. With C16 KV / TP1 / 32K / max_num_seqs=4, four-client variable-prompt ordinary-text and strict JSON Schema smoke tests passed **16/16**. Requests exceeding the single-request graph capture range run eagerly; this is not a claim of multi-request model Graph coverage or general accuracy.
- The experimental C8 adapter is single-request-only and explicitly rejected a multi-request candidate; that limitation is outside this GDN fix.
- `bash format.sh ci` and `git diff --check` passed. Full model/task accuracy, long-context validation and performance benchmarking were not performed for this fix.

Original failing-kernel reproduction, numerical logs and model smoke evidence: [reproduction report](https://github.com/ychy7001/ascend310p-qwen36/blob/dbb9e00/docs/gdn-17856-reproduction.md), [raw results](https://github.com/ychy7001/ascend310p-qwen36/tree/dbb9e00/results/gdn-17856-20261014). This does not establish that the bug caused previously observed MTP acceptance-rate changes.

Review follow-up: `70ccf5c85` promotes the writeback state index to `uint64_t` before multiplication. The rebuilt 310P operator passed the same three pytest modes (126 output/state checks). This regression checks ordinary-sized state pools; it does not allocate a pool large enough to exercise the theoretical 32-bit overflow threshold. Latest upstream main `8783fc6` was merged without changes to the tested GDN runtime files.

items.title: [Performance][MRV2] Skip seq-lens D2H sync for device-native backends under spec decoding via consumer-declared requirement
items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?
Implements the MRV2 portion of the host sequence-length data contract (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/17479).

Under async scheduling + speculative decoding, MRV2 unconditionally staged a D2H copy of `num_computed_tokens` after rejection sampling and waited on it at the start of the next input preparation — even for attention backends that consume exact sequence lengths entirely on device (DSA/SFA/GDN). The host wait serializes CPU preparation behind NPU completion of the previous step, which removes the CPU/NPU overlap that async scheduling exists to provide and leaves NPU bubbles.

This PR makes the dependency consumer-declared instead of unconditional:

- New `HostSeqLensRequirement` contract (`NONE` / `UPPER_BOUND` / `EXACT`) in `vllm_ascend/attention/utils.py`. Builders declare what they actually consume via a `HOST_SEQ_LENS_REQUIREMENT` class attribute; undeclared builders conservatively fall back to `EXACT` with a one-time warning.
- MRV2 aggregates the strongest requirement over target and draft (speculator) metadata builders after KV-cache init, and stages the snapshot / waits only under `EXACT`.
- Consumer classification:
  - `EXACT`: legacy FIA (`AscendAttentionMetadataBuilder`, inherited by FA3/PCP/DCP/C8 variants), MLA (`AscendMLAMetadataBuilder`), MiniMax-M3 (its prefill path still syncs context lengths on host)
  - `UPPER_BOUND`: DSA, SFA, GDN (host view only feeds workspace/tiling hints or prefill/decode classification, both tolerant of a conservative bound)
  - `NONE`: SFA indexer (device seq_lens only)
- Hybrid models are safe by construction: a single `EXACT` consumer forces exact materialization for the whole execution (e.g. Qwen3-Next FIA+GDN).

Behavior is unchanged for `EXACT` executions (incl. non-spec-decode serving); device-native executions (e.g. DeepSeek-V4 + DSpark) now run with zero seq-lens D2H transfers and zero host waits.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No.

### How was this patch tested?

- UT: `tests/ut/attention/test_seq_lens_requirement.py` (aggregation takes strongest requirement, hybrid safety, undeclared fallback, subclass inheritance, draft participation, in-tree declaration guard)
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DSpark MTP, TP4/DP4, async scheduling:
  - startup diagnostic shows `requirement=UPPER_BOUND, undeclared=[]`
  - greedy outputs identical to main (token-exact)
  - profiling: the seq-lens host wait is gone; NPU bubble eliminated

items.title: [Performance][Triton] Optimize gated LayerNorm row tiling and parameter reuse
items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Gated RMSNorm is used in the GDN output projection of [Qwen3.5-27B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-27B/blob/af65380a20d418eeb0a2bcb784dd43e9b76c4a2e/config.json) and [Qwen3.5-35B-A3B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B/blob/41adbc1e50345066ac5153217957e9910204e632/config.json), both with value-head width 128. vLLM's [Qwen3.5 linear-attention layers](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_5.py#L144-L151) use Qwen GDN, whose [output norm](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607/vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py#L487-L494) sets `group_size=None` and `norm_before_gate=True`. The [Ascend GDN path](https://github.com/c5566b/vllm-ascend/blob/1097a8d766ec8abb4e3bfb9fba72b10bbe0beeb2/vllm_ascend/ops/gdn.py#L333-L341) flattens this output to `[M,128]`, and the [gated-norm wrapper](https://github.com/c5566b/vllm-ascend/blob/1097a8d766ec8abb4e3bfb9fba72b10bbe0beeb2/vllm_ascend/ops/layernorm.py#L138-L147) calls `layer_norm_fwd_npu`, giving the single-group N128 workload optimized here. [OLMo-Hybrid-7B](https://huggingface.co/allenai/Olmo-Hybrid-7B/blob/712e06263b8656a2ea6ec2c395106f19bba2f50f/config.json) uses value-head width 192 through [gated RMSNorm](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607/vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/olmo_gdn_linear_attn.py#L149-L157), motivating the wider resource control below.

Here `M` is the row count and `N_group` is the normalization width per group. The existing full-tile kernel processes 64 rows per program. This fixed row block has different costs as the workload changes: small M exposes few independent row blocks, wider `N_group` increases the tile's UB demand, and large M launches many programs that each reload the same weight and optional bias. In the N192 control below, BASE64 requires 321 KiB on a 192 KiB UB target.

This PR adjusts the row block and execution organization while preserving the normalization and gating math. For single-group inputs, smaller BASE tiles expose more independent work at small M and reduce full-tile resource demand at wider N, allowing the measured N192 inputs to compile and run. For suitable single-group N128 workloads, HOIST32 bounds the grid by the initialized vector-core count and uses a grid-stride loop over BM32 row blocks. Weight and optional bias are loaded outside that loop and reused when a program processes multiple blocks. The two NPU kernel implementations are the existing BASE kernel, launched with BM16 or BM64, and HOIST32 with BM32, persistent execution, and parameter reuse.

Dispatch retains BASE64 for all multi-group inputs (`G>1`). For single-group NPU inputs, it chooses a path by group width and row-tile count. At widths 129–512, BASE16 requires the existing UB getter to report at least 192 KiB. The core selector below omits input validation and expands constants for readability. `LaunchSpec` specifies the kernel implementation and row-block size; `ngroups` is `G`, and `runtime_p` is the worker-initialized vector-core count. The wrapper queries these NPU properties only for single-group calls; non-NPU calls supply `runtime_p=None` and retain BASE64.

```python
def _select_layernorm_launch(M, N_group, ngroups, runtime_p, *, ub_bytes=None):
    if ngroups > 1 or runtime_p is None:
        return LaunchSpec("FT_BASE", 64)  # BASE64: retain baseline

    if N_group > 128:
        if N_group <= 512 and ub_bytes is not None and ub_bytes >= 196_608:
            return LaunchSpec("FT_BASE", 16)  # BASE16: smaller full tile
        return LaunchSpec("FT_BASE", 64)

    if N_group < 128:
        return LaunchSpec("FT_BASE", 16)  # BASE16

    # Single group, N_group == 128
    hoist_tiles = (M + 32 - 1) // 32
    if 4 * hoist_tiles >= runtime_p:
        return LaunchSpec("FT_PERSIST_HOIST", 32)  # HOIST32
    return LaunchSpec("FT_BASE", 16)
```

For single-group N128, the rule selects HOIST32 when the BM32 tile count covers at least one quarter of the initialized vector cores. This is a compact policy supported by the measured cases. The large-M comparisons below show why smaller BASE tiles alone do not replace HOIST32's persistent execution and parameter reuse.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This is an internal kernel and launch optimization. The public API, calling convention, input/output contract, and normalization/gating semantics remain unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

Tested on Ascend910B4 with 40 vector cores, 192 KiB UB, and CANN 8.5.

- Host unit tests cover dispatch boundaries, grouped BASE64 fallback, the wide-N UB guard, and wrapper launch arguments.
- BF16/FP16 outputs and applicable statistics passed CPU-reference checks, including single-group BASE16 at N192/256/384/512. All three routes in the performance table passed numerical checks with identical inputs, and their launch configurations were verified.

**Performance.** The N128 cases follow Qwen3.5 GDN's norm-before-gating semantics and cover small M, the dispatch boundary, tails, and larger workloads. Each route cell shows **median device time (us) / speedup relative to BASE64 (`1.000x`)**, measured with `msprof op`. `G` is the group count. Bold cells indicate the route selected by dispatch.

| M | N_group | G | Dtype | Norm | z / bias | norm_before_gate | BASE64 (frozen baseline) | BASE16 (route 1) | HOIST32 (route 2) | Selected route |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 128 | 128 | 1 | BF16 | RMSNorm | Yes / No | True (post-gate) | 8.310 / 1.000x | **5.590 / 1.487x** | 6.030 / 1.378x | **BASE16** |
| 288 | 128 | 1 | BF16 | RMSNorm | Yes / No | True (post-gate) | 7.670 / 1.000x | **6.430 / 1.193x** | 6.550 / 1.171x | **BASE16** |
| 289 | 128 | 1 | BF16 | RMSNorm | Yes / No | True (post-gate) | 7.440 / 1.000x | 6.600 / 1.127x | **6.620 / 1.124x** | **HOIST32** |
| 639 | 128 | 1 | BF16 | RMSNorm | Yes / No | True (post-gate) | 7.750 / 1.000x | 8.190 / 0.946x | **7.530 / 1.029x** | **HOIST32** |
| 20449 | 128 | 1 | BF16 | RMSNorm | Yes / No | True (post-gate) | 53.121 / 1.000x | 142.033 / 0.374x | **41.071 / 1.293x** | **HOIST32** |
| 65536 | 128 | 1 | BF16 | RMSNorm | Yes / No | True (post-gate) | 160.553 / 1.000x | 444.989 / 0.361x | **117.612 / 1.365x** | **HOIST32** |

The selected routes improve over frozen BASE64 at all six measured shapes. BASE16 benefits small M; near the dispatch boundary, BASE16 and HOIST32 have similar timings. At the larger M20449 and M65536 points, HOIST32 outperforms both BASE64 and BASE16, supporting persistent execution and parameter reuse alongside smaller BASE tiles.

**UB resource controls.** M60/N192 uses OLMo's value-head width of 192. BF16 RMSNorm with `z` and no bias was tested with identical baseline/PR1 inputs for both gate orders in the same B4/P40 environment.

| M | N_group | G | norm_before_gate | Upstream BASE64 (BM64/BN256) | Public PR1 BASE16 (BM16/BN256) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 60 | 192 | 1 | True (post-gate) | Compile failed: 321 KiB required > 192 KiB available | Compiled; numerical checks passed |
| 60 | 192 | 1 | False (pre-gate) | Compile failed: 321 KiB required > 192 KiB available | Compiled; numerical checks passed |

These measurements cover unchanged single-group kernels and launch configurations; the later grouped-fallback wrapper revision has not been rerun on device. Interface constraints and correctness-test coverage are described in the [operator documentation](https://github.com/c5566b/vllm-ascend/blob/7bb286f5eba473ce53733c23f64112433c6822b7/vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/layernorm_gated.md).

In-tree NPU CI/Nightly and integration remain pending. The earlier M288 first-launch NaN did not recur in the final tests; its cause remains unresolved.
